title: Derivatives metrics: open interest, funding, liquidations and basis
body:
## Context
R2 "Order-flow beta" (`docs/plan/30-release-roadmap.md#6-r2--order-flow-beta`, sprints S10-S13, tag `v0.3.0`, staging/demo) delivers DeepCharts-grade order-flow visibility. **E24 Derivatives metrics (OI, funding, liquidations, basis)** is the *positioning and carry* layer of that release. Roadmap scope line (§6.2): "Open-interest series with delta-OI; funding rate current + history + countdown using the `fundingInterval` actually read from instruments-info (not assumed 8 h); liquidation feed and liquidation-cluster overlay; basis vs index/mark; OI-vs-price quadrant classification (long build-up / short build-up / long liquidation / short covering)" - **34 pts, sprints S12-S13**, area `area/order-flow`, backend modules **M4** (ingestion/normalisation of the public `tickers` + `allLiquidation` streams, owned by E08) and **M9** (`server/orderflow/`, the derived-series engines), story domain **DERIV**.

Three facts from the plan documents shape every ticket in this epic and must not be re-litigated during implementation:

1. **The funding interval is instrument data, never a constant.** `docs/plan/22-api-openapi.yaml` `/market/funding` states it verbatim: "The funding interval is instrument-specific (`funding_interval_minutes`; 8 h common, some 1/2/4 h) - never assume 8 h." The value is read from the cached instruments-info snapshot (`GET /api/v1/instruments`, field `funding_interval_minutes`; Postgres `instruments.funding_interval_min` default 480) and is used for the countdown, the annualisation factor and the `funding_8h` session anchor alike.
2. **There is no exchange history endpoint for liquidations.** `docs/plan/21-database-schema.md` §4.6: "No REST history exists for liquidations - depth is strictly bounded by recorder uptime; the UI must state this." Every liquidation surface therefore renders the partial-history state naming the first available timestamp (R2 exit criterion #5), and `GET /api/v1/market/liquidations` reads only the locally recorded `liquidations` QuestDB table populated from `allLiquidation.{symbol}` (the legacy `liquidation` topic is retired).
3. **Liquidation heat / cluster zones are an inference, not exchange data.** US-DERIV-007's NFR: "never presented as exchange-provided data; excluded from any automated rule action by default." It therefore carries the mandatory CMP-227 `(estimated)` badge, is **off by default**, and links the methodology drawer SCR-058 (global AC #6, R2 exit criterion #4 - "A missing badge is a P1 bug, not cosmetic").

Everything numeric in this epic is a first-class `MetricDescriptor` in the `MetricRegistry` (`docs/plan/24-internal-schemas.md` §7 "Derivatives"): `open_interest`, `open_interest_value`, `open_interest_delta`, `oi_price_quadrant` (`long_buildup|short_covering|short_buildup|long_unwind`), `funding_rate`, `funding_annualized`, `time_to_funding_ms`, `basis`, `premium_pct`, `liquidation_notional`. That is the single-source invariant of R2: a rule, an alert and a derivatives pane always read the same number. There is exactly one `DerivativesEngine` in M9 and the UI is a renderer of its output - a second client-side computation of basis, annualised funding or OI delta is an explicit anti-goal.

Dependency per the roadmap graph (§11.1): `E08 --> E24`. E08 Bybit adapter & ingestion skeleton owns the `tickers` stream normalisation (delta ticker frames merged against last full state before write, `21-database-schema.md` §4.4) and the public-stream connection manager that the liquidation socket plugs into. E16 Recorder supplies liquidation persistence and history depth (US-DERIV-005 `Deps: US-REC-001`). E11/E12 supply the chart-engine sub-pane, shared time axis and crosshair sync that US-DERIV-008's NFR requires ("all derivative series respect the same time axis and crosshair sync as price"). E17 owns the WS envelope/topic registry that `ticker.{symbol}` and `liquidations.{symbol}` live in.

## Scope / Deliverables
- **User stories covered (all 8 of the DERIV domain, `docs/plan/11-user-stories.md` §14):** US-DERIV-001 (Must, OI pane), US-DERIV-002 (Should, OI delta + price quadrant colouring), US-DERIV-003 (Must, funding rate/history/countdown), US-DERIV-004 (Should, predicted & annualised funding), US-DERIV-005 (Must, liquidation feed), US-DERIV-006 (Must, liquidation bars), US-DERIV-007 (Should, liquidation heat / cluster estimate), US-DERIV-008 (Should, basis, mark/index and long/short ratio).
- **Screens:** SCR-054 OI / funding / liquidations panel (the epic's home screen, `docs/plan/14-screens-catalogue.md#scr-054`); SCR-058 Detector methodology drawer (new entry for the liquidation-cluster heuristic); SCR-030 Chart panel hosts the liquidation markers and the sub-pane.
- **Components:** CMP-186 OiFundingLiqPane (chart primitive), CMP-126 FundingCountdown, CMP-127 LiquidationMarker, CMP-036 KeyValueRow, CMP-188 PriceAxis, CMP-199 ChartLegend, CMP-227 EstimatedBadge.
- **Backend (M4 + M9):** liquidation socket + normaliser and OI/funding extraction from the merged ticker snapshot (M4); `DerivativesEngine` (M9) computing OI delta, the OI/price quadrant, basis/premium, annualised funding, per-bar liquidation notional and the estimated liquidation-cluster bands; metric descriptors registered in the `MetricRegistry`.
- **Contracts:** REST `GET /api/v1/market/open-interest`, `GET /api/v1/market/funding`, `GET /api/v1/market/liquidations`, `GET /api/v1/market/metrics` (metrics `open_interest_delta`, `funding_basis`, `liquidation_intensity` and the derivatives descriptors), `GET /api/v1/instruments/{symbol}`; WS topics `ticker.{symbol}` / `ticker` (`TickerUpdate`, `23-ws-protocol.md` §14.8) and `liquidations.{symbol}` / `liquidations` (`LiquidationBatch`, §14.9, options `min_notional_usd`, `cluster_window_ms`).
- **Data:** QuestDB `tickers` (`open_interest`, `open_interest_value`, `funding_rate`, `next_funding_ts`, `basis`), `open_interest`, `funding_rates`, `liquidations` (`21-database-schema.md` §4.4-4.7); Postgres `instruments.funding_interval_min`, `settings` (scope `user`, keys `deriv.*`) for pane configuration and threshold memory; `stream_kind` enum values `liquidations`, `open_interest`, `funding` for recorder policy.
- **Design:** full design track for SCR-054, CMP-186/CMP-126/CMP-127 and the SCR-058 methodology entry, scheduled S10-S11 (>=2 sprints ahead of the S12-S13 engineering work), plus a design-QA sweep in S13.
- **QA:** black-box plan + exploratory charter, Playwright E2E additions, a liquidation-cascade perf script (500 prints/s sustained for 10 s), chaos scenarios (ticker staleness, REST backfill failure), a11y audit, epic regression pack and sign-off.
- **Security:** STRIDE model for the epic and a review of the backfill/pagination/estimation surfaces.

## Out of scope
- Options / GEX data - explicitly out of scope per the locked decisions in `docs/plan/00-planning-brief.md`.
- Non-USDT-perp instruments and non-Bybit venues; the exchange-adapter abstraction is E08's.
- Funding-cost accounting against real positions (`funding_paid` on `trades_journal`) - E41 Journal.
- Alert conditions built on derivatives metrics (alert centre, notification routing) - E40 Alerts; this epic only guarantees the metrics are registered and queryable.
- Rule-engine actions driven by OI/funding - E35; and by explicit NFR the estimated liquidation zones are excluded from automated rule actions by default.
- The liquidation-price line for the *user's own position* (SCR-063 trading overlays, CMP-127 in its position sense) - E31/E32.
- CVD, footprint, profiles, DOM heatmap, detectors, replay - E18/E19/E21/E23/E25/E26.
- Android and a separate admin app.

## Acceptance criteria
```gherkin
Scenario: One engine, one number
  Given the DerivativesEngine has computed open_interest_delta and basis for BTCUSDT bar 10:35
  When the SCR-054 pane, a GET /api/v1/market/metrics query and a rule condition each read those metrics
  Then all three return byte-identical values for the same bar and params
  And no derivatives value is recomputed client-side

Scenario: The funding interval is never assumed
  Given a symbol whose instruments-info funding_interval_minutes is 240
  When the funding countdown, the annualised rate and the funding history render
  Then all three use 240 minutes (6 settlements/day, annualisation factor 1460)
  And no code path contains a hard-coded 8-hour or 480-minute default outside the instruments table column default

Scenario: Honest liquidation history
  Given the recorder for BTCUSDT started 2 hours ago
  When I open the liquidation bars for a 24-hour range
  Then bars exist only for the recorded window, a boundary marker names the first available timestamp
  And the panel states that no exchange history endpoint exists for liquidations

Scenario: Estimated zones are labelled and off by default
  Given a fresh installation
  When I open SCR-054
  Then liquidation heat/cluster zones are disabled
  And enabling them requires acknowledging that the values are estimated
  And once enabled every zone renders a CMP-227 (estimated) badge linking SCR-058

Scenario: Cascade does not drop frames
  Given a liquidation cascade producing 500 prints/second for 10 seconds
  When the feed and the liquidation bars are both visible
  Then prints are coalesced into 250 ms buckets with a burst counter
  And panel scripting stays under 2 ms per frame with no dropped frames
```

## Technical notes / design
- **Module split.** M4 (ingestion) is responsible only for *sockets and normalisation*: the `allLiquidation.{symbol}` subscription, and extracting `openInterest`/`openInterestValue`/`fundingRate`/`nextFundingTime`/`markPrice`/`indexPrice` from the merged ticker snapshot. M9 (`orderflow`) hosts `DerivativesEngine`, which is pure and testable: `(ticker snapshots, funding rows, liquidation prints, bar grid, instrument metadata) -> metric series`. No HTTP or socket code inside M9.
- **OI resolution.** Two sources with different cadences coexist in the `open_interest` table, distinguished by `(interval, source)` in the dedup key: `source='rest'` rows at 5min..1d from `GET /v5/market/open-interest` (limit <=200/page), and `source='ws_ticker'` rows at 1 s derived from the recorded `tickers` stream. The UI never silently mixes them: when the chart interval is finer than the native REST granularity the pane shows the "native granularity 5 min" note (US-DERIV-001).
- **Quadrant classification** (`24-internal-schemas.md` §7, research 08 §6): price up + OI up = `long_buildup`; price up + OI down = `short_covering`; price down + OI up = `short_buildup`; price down + OI down = `long_unwind`. A bar with no OI sample is `None` - drawn neutral-hatched and excluded from classification, never defaulted to a quadrant.
- **Annualisation.** `funding_annualized = funding_rate * (525600 / funding_interval_minutes)`; `funding_rates.annualised_pct` stores it precomputed. Predicted (unsettled) rates come only from the ticker `fundingRate` field and are flagged `predicted: true, estimated: true` by `/market/funding`; the UI must render them in a visually distinct, text-labelled style and show `n/a` rather than a stale value when absent.
- **Basis.** `basis = last - index` (or `mark - index` when `source=mark`), `premium_pct = basis / index * 100`; `tickers.basis` is precomputed at ingest so `ASOF JOIN` queries stay cheap.
- **Liquidation clustering.** Two distinct things share the word "cluster": (a) `cluster_size` on `LiquidationBatch` / `cluster_window_ms` on `/market/liquidations`, which is *exact* grouping of prints within a time window - not estimated; (b) the liquidation *heat/zone* estimate of US-DERIV-007, derived from OI, leverage tiers and price distance - always estimated, off by default, documented in SCR-058.
- **Burst handling.** Bybit pushes `allLiquidation` at most once per symbol per 500 ms, so event counts are lower bounds - the UI states this. Client-side prints are coalesced into 250 ms buckets with a burst-rate counter rather than one DOM node per print (`14-screens-catalogue.md` SCR-054 performance note).
- **Config keys** (Postgres `settings`, scope `user`): `deriv.oi.mode` (`absolute|delta`), `deriv.oi.quadrant_colouring`, `deriv.funding.style` (`line|bars`), `deriv.funding.annualised`, `deriv.liq.mode` (`bars|heatmap`), `deriv.liq.min_notional_usd`, `deriv.liq.zones_enabled` (default `false`), `deriv.basis.source` (`last|mark`), `deriv.basis.annualised`.
- **Error codes:** reuse the standard envelope; backfill failure surfaces as a retryable pane state carrying `last_success_at`, never a blank chart (US-DERIV-008 scenario 3).

## Test plan
- **Unit (>=85%):** quadrant classification truth table incl. the `None` case; annualisation across 1 h/2 h/4 h/8 h intervals; basis/premium; per-bar liquidation notional bucketing incl. day-boundary alignment; countdown arithmetic against a skewed clock offset; coalescing buffer.
- **Contract:** OpenAPI schema tests for `/market/open-interest`, `/market/funding`, `/market/liquidations`, `/market/metrics`; WS JSON-schema validation of `TickerUpdate` and `LiquidationBatch`.
- **Integration:** recorded Bybit fixtures - normal session, cascade burst, ticker delta-merge sequence, REST backfill 5xx/rate-limit (10018), symbol with a 4 h funding interval.
- **E2E (Playwright):** open SCR-054, toggle OI absolute/delta, enable quadrant colouring, switch funding style + annualise, filter liquidations by notional, enable estimated zones through the acknowledgement, verify partial-history chip.
- **Perf:** 500 prints/s for 10 s with panel scripting <2 ms/frame; WS tick -> screen p95 <100 ms with the heaviest topic set including `ticker` + `liquidations` (budget #3, R2 hard gate).
- **Chaos:** ticker socket drop and resubscribe; REST backfill failure; clock-offset jump during a countdown.
- **Golden fixture:** a recorded symbol-day recomputed offline in DuckDB over the Parquet tier must match the engine's OI delta, basis, annualised funding and per-bar liquidation notional within float tolerance (R2 exit criterion #6 extended to derivatives).

## Security notes
Data classification: public market data only - no secrets, PII or account data flows through this epic, which keeps the threat surface narrow. Threats from `docs/plan/04-security-program.md` worth modelling: (T) tampering via a fabricated predicted-funding or estimated-zone value presented as exchange data - mitigated by the mandatory `estimated`/`predicted` flags at the schema level, not only in the UI; (I) information disclosure is nil-risk here but the endpoints still require `marketdata:read` per their `x-rbac` blocks and must not become an unauthenticated path; (D) denial of service via unbounded `from`/`to` ranges or `limit` on the three REST endpoints, and via a client subscribing `liquidations` with `symbols` over the cap - mitigated by pagination caps, cursor enforcement and subscription limits; (R) repudiation of "the tool told me OI was rising" - mitigated by recording the source (`ws_ticker` vs `rest`) on every stored point. A `security` review ticket (E24-X02) and a STRIDE model (E24-X01) are in scope.

## Accessibility notes
Per `docs/plan/05-accessibility-standard.md` and SCR-054's catalogue entry: every sub-pane has a **table alternative** (the DOM-mirror pattern) so the data is readable without the canvas; the funding countdown is announced at 5 min and 1 min only (never per second); quadrant classification is conveyed by pattern + text legend, never colour alone; the `(estimated)` badge carries the literal word "estimated" in its accessible name (CMP-227 contract); liquidation side is labelled in text, not only by red/green; all controls are keyboard reachable with visible focus; contrast >=4.5:1 for text and >=3:1 for the pane's graphical boundaries in both themes.

## Performance notes
Budgets from `docs/plan/06-performance-and-load-standard.md`: #1 frame time p95 <=16.6 ms with the full order-flow scene including this pane; #2 never below 30 fps in degraded mode; #3 WS tick -> screen p95 <100 ms / p99 <250 ms (hard R2 gate). SCR-054 specific: OI and funding arrive at <=1 Hz and render on change only; liquidation prints coalesce into 250 ms buckets; the panel must not exceed **2 ms scripting per frame** during a cascade (500 prints/s sustained for 10 s, no dropped frames). REST backfill paging must respect Bybit's <=200 rows/page limit and stay inside the API read budget (#13, p95 <150 ms backend-internal).

## Observability
Metrics: `deriv_oi_backfill_pages_total{symbol,result}`, `deriv_oi_backfill_latency_seconds`, `deriv_funding_refresh_total{result}`, `deriv_liquidation_prints_total{symbol,side}`, `deriv_liquidation_burst_rate`, `deriv_ticker_staleness_seconds{symbol}`, `deriv_engine_compute_seconds{metric}`. Logs: structured warning on backfill failure with `symbol`, `interval`, `attempt`, `http_status`; warning when a ticker snapshot is stale beyond threshold. Traces: span per backfill job and per metric batch. Audit/analytics events from SCR-054: `oi_panel.metric_toggled`, `oi_panel.interval_changed`, plus a dedicated event when the estimated-zone acknowledgement is accepted.

## Definition of Done
- [ ] All child Stories/Tasks/Spikes/Design/QA/Security tickets Done (100% rollup) or explicitly descoped with a recorded disposition.
- [ ] All 8 DERIV stories demonstrably satisfied end-to-end on SCR-054 against a recorded symbol-day.
- [ ] Coverage >=85% on `server/orderflow/derivatives*` and the ingestion additions, >=80% on the frontend pane.
- [ ] `22-api-openapi.yaml`, `23-ws-protocol.md`, `24-internal-schemas.md`, `14-screens-catalogue.md` SCR-054/SCR-058 reflect shipped behaviour; ADR-0017 merged.
- [ ] a11y: axe-core green on SCR-054, one manual screen-reader pass, table alternatives verified.
- [ ] perf: cascade benchmark and WS tick->screen p95 recorded against budgets #1/#3.
- [ ] security: STRIDE finalised, findings triaged, Security engineer sign-off comment.
- [ ] design: SCR-054 and CMP-186/126/127 signed off by the CDO track; design-QA sweep closed.
- [ ] QA: epic-level regression + exploratory pass recorded; zero open P0/P1.
- [ ] Demoed to the Owner at Sprint Review with explicit acceptance recorded.

## Dependencies
- **E08 Bybit adapter & ingestion skeleton** (`E08 --> E24` in the roadmap graph): ticker delta-merge normalisation, public-stream connection manager, instruments-info cache with `funding_interval_minutes`.
- **E16 Recorder, retention & disk budget**: liquidation persistence and the recorded-history depth every liquidation view depends on (US-DERIV-005 `Deps: US-REC-001`).
- **E17 Market-data WS protocol & binary framing**: envelope, subscription lifecycle and topic registry for `ticker.*` / `liquidations.*`.
- **E11/E12 chart engine**: sub-pane hosting, shared time axis, crosshair sync, pane legend.
- **E05 Design system v0**: tokens and primitives the new components build on.

## Branch
`feat/e24-derivatives-*` per child ticket (e.g. `feat/e24-derivatives-oi-backfill`). PR size guidance: <=400 LOC diff; the engine, the endpoints and each pane surface are separate PRs.

## Agent guidance

How to pick the next ticket in this epic when multiple agents are working it in parallel:

1. **Design track first** (E24-D01, E24-D02, E24-D03, E24-D04, E24-D05, E24-D06) must clear the design-ahead rule (Done ≥2 sprints before the Story that consumes it) before any Story in its lane starts — check each Story's own `blocked_by` for the exact design ticket.
2. **Spike/engineering foundation** (E24-K01, E24-T01, E24-T02, E24-T03, E24-T04, E24-T05, E24-T06) generally has no ticket dependency on the Stories and can start immediately in parallel with design — these define the wire contract and backend engines the Stories consume.
3. **Stories** (E24-S01, E24-S02, E24-S03, E24-S04, E24-S05, E24-S06, E24-S07, E24-S08) are blocked by their named Task/Spike and design ticket per each Story's own `blocked_by` list — do not start a Story until every key in its `blocked_by` is Done.
4. **QA** (E24-Q01, E24-Q02, E24-Q03, E24-Q04, E24-Q05) and **Security** (E24-X01, E24-X02) tracks run against the Stories/Tasks they test — pick these up once their named inputs are Done, not before.
5. **Parallel lanes**: two agents may safely work any two tickets that do not appear in each other's `blocked_by` chain and do not touch the same repo paths in the same PR window — check both before starting.
6. **Shared interfaces to agree first**: any change to a WS topic, REST path, DB table, or `MetricRegistry`/`MetricDescriptor` entry named across multiple children must be raised and agreed (PR to `22-api-openapi.yaml` / `23-ws-protocol.md` / `24-internal-schemas.md`) before two agents implement against diverging assumptions.

title: UX research: how perp traders read OI, funding and liquidations
body:
## Context
SCR-054 packs four semantically different derivative signals (positioning, carry, forced flow and the spot/perp spread) into one narrow panel. Before wireframing we need evidence on the questions traders actually ask of those numbers, so the panel is ordered by decision value rather than by data availability. The epic covers US-DERIV-001..008 (`docs/plan/11-user-stories.md` §14) and the panel is the only home screen for all eight.

## Scope / Deliverables
- 4-5 moderated sessions with the Owner and the account managers (the only real users - `docs/plan/10-personas.md`), using a recorded BTCUSDT symbol-day that contains a funding settlement and a liquidation cascade.
- Probe: absolute OI vs OI delta as the default view; whether quadrant classification (`long_buildup|short_covering|short_buildup|long_unwind`) is understood without a legend; what the funding countdown must say at <5 min; whether liquidation bars or a feed is the primary surface; whether the basis pane is a peer pane or a header readout.
- Probe the honesty affordances: does the partial-history chip ("history starts <ts>") actually stop mis-reads, and does the `(estimated)` badge on liquidation zones read as a warning or as decoration.
- Deliverable: a research brief in Figma/Confluence with prioritised findings, a recommended default pane order and default settings values for the `deriv.*` keys, and 3-5 explicit design implications carried into E24-D02.

## Out of scope
Visual design, tokens, prototypes; detector methodology copy (SCR-058 is E25's home but this epic adds its liquidation-cluster section, drafted in E24-K01); research on CVD/footprint panes.

## Acceptance criteria
```gherkin
Scenario: Sessions completed
  Given the recorded symbol-day fixture with a funding settlement and a cascade
  When 4 or more sessions have been run
  Then a research brief exists with prioritised findings and a recommended default pane order

Scenario: Defaults are evidence-backed
  When the brief recommends default values for deriv.oi.mode, deriv.funding.annualised, deriv.liq.mode and deriv.liq.min_notional_usd
  Then each recommendation cites at least one observed session behaviour

Scenario: Honesty affordances tested
  When participants are shown the partial-history chip and the (estimated) badge
  Then the brief records whether each was noticed and correctly interpreted
  And any participant who read an estimated zone as exchange data is recorded as a blocking finding for E24-D03

Scenario: No participants available
  Given the Owner and managers cannot be scheduled inside the sprint
  Then the brief is produced from a heuristic walkthrough of TradingView/Coinglass equivalents with the limitation stated on its first page, and the ticket is still closed rather than blocking E24-D02
```

## Technical notes / design
Method: think-aloud over a clickable static fixture (no live data, no build dependency). Record with consent; store notes in the design repo, no account data captured. Synthesis uses affinity mapping; findings are tagged with the US id they affect so E24-D02 can trace each wireframe decision back to a finding.

## Test plan
N/A - research artefact. Validation is the CDO review of the brief.

## Security notes
No production data, no credentials and no account identifiers are captured; recordings contain public market data only and are deleted after synthesis per `docs/plan/04-security-program.md` data-handling rules.

## Accessibility notes
The research explicitly includes one pass with the panel's table alternative and keyboard-only operation, so accessibility is a design input rather than a retrofit (`docs/plan/05-accessibility-standard.md` §11.3).

## Performance notes
N/A

## Observability
N/A - no runtime component.

## Definition of Done
- [ ] 4+ sessions run (or the documented fallback used).
- [ ] Research brief published and linked from this ticket and from E24-D02.
- [ ] Findings tagged per US-DERIV-00x.
- [ ] CDO review comment recorded.
- [ ] Recommended `deriv.*` defaults handed to E24-D02 and E24-S01/S03/S05.

## Dependencies
None. Feeds E24-D02 (wireframes), which must not start before the brief is reviewed.

## Branch
`design/e24-deriv-research` (artefacts only, no code). PR size: docs only.

## References
- `docs/plan/11-user-stories.md` §14 DERIV

title: Motion spec and accessibility review for the derivatives panel
body:
## Context
SCR-054 has three moving things - a per-second countdown, low-frequency OI/funding updates and bursty liquidation prints - plus a pane whose data can go stale. Motion here is a legibility tool, not decoration: an unthrottled cascade animation is both a perf hazard and an a11y hazard. This ticket fixes the motion contract and runs the formal accessibility review of the hi-fi before handoff.

## Scope / Deliverables
- Motion spec: countdown tick (text swap, no animation), value-change flash on OI/funding (<=120 ms, `prefers-reduced-motion` removes it entirely), liquidation bucket entry animation capped at the 250 ms coalescing cadence, stale-data shading fade, pane collapse/expand easing and duration, zone-overlay fade on enable.
- Explicit rule: nothing animates faster than the data's own cadence; during a cascade the bucket animation is suppressed rather than queued.
- Accessibility review of the E24-D03 hi-fi: focus order across the three sub-panes and the settings surface, keyboard path to every control, live-region policy (countdown announced at 5 min and 1 min only - never per second, per the SCR-054 catalogue entry), announcement throttling for bursty liquidations, table-alternative column semantics and units, non-colour encoding of quadrant and side.
- An a11y annotation layer on the Figma frames that engineering can read directly (roles, names, live-region politeness, tab order numbers).

## Out of scope
Implementation; axe automation (E24-Q04 runs the audit on the built panel).

## Acceptance criteria
```gherkin
Scenario: Reduced motion
  Given prefers-reduced-motion: reduce
  Then every flash, fade and bucket animation is removed and only instantaneous state changes remain, with no loss of information

Scenario: Countdown announcements
  When a screen reader is on and the funding countdown is running
  Then it is announced at 5 minutes and at 1 minute remaining only, and never once per second

Scenario: Cascade announcements
  Given 500 liquidation prints per second
  Then announcements are throttled to at most one summary every 5 seconds naming the burst rate, not one per print

Scenario: Keyboard completeness
  When the panel is operated by keyboard only
  Then every control including the sub-pane collapse, the mode toggles, the threshold input and the zone acknowledgement is reachable with a visible focus indicator

Scenario: Annotation coverage
  When an engineer opens the hi-fi
  Then every interactive element carries a role, an accessible name and a tab-order number
```

## Technical notes / design
Durations and easings come from the motion tokens in `docs/plan/16-design-system-brief.md`. The live-region policy is specified as a concrete rule set (politeness, throttle window, message template) so E24-S03/S05 implement it verbatim rather than improvising.

## Test plan
Reviewed with a screen-reader specialist against the annotation layer; the throttle rules are handed to E24-Q04 as audit checkpoints.

## Security notes

title: Spike: liquidation-zone estimation methodology and its honesty limits
body:
## Context
US-DERIV-007 asks for "estimated zones derived from OI, leverage tiers and price distance". Bybit publishes neither per-account leverage nor a liquidation-price distribution, so any zone is an inference over aggregate OI plus assumed leverage buckets. Before a line of engine code is written we must decide whether an honest version of this feature is possible at all, what inputs it uses, and exactly what it may and may not claim. The epic's cross-cutting caveat (`docs/plan/14-screens-catalogue.md` §0.5 rule 2 and US-DERIV-007's NFR) makes the wrong answer a correctness bug, not a tuning issue.

## Scope / Deliverables
- Evaluate 2-3 candidate methods over recorded symbol-days: (a) OI-weighted leverage-bucket projection - distribute current `open_interest` across assumed leverage tiers (10x/25x/50x/100x) and map each tier to a maintenance-margin distance from a reference price, using the instruments-info risk-limit tiers cached by E08; (b) realised-liquidation histogram - cluster the recorded `liquidations` table by price to show where forced flow has actually occurred (exact, not estimated); (c) a hybrid rendering (b) as the primary surface and (a) as an optional overlay.
- Backtest: for each method, measure how often a projected zone precedes an actual recorded liquidation cluster within N ticks and M minutes, on at least three symbol-days including one cascade.
- Decide the default: whether zones ship at all, and if so which method, which parameters, and which claims the SCR-058 copy may make.
- Measure the compute cost of the chosen method per bar-grid update so E24-S07 has a budget.
- Output: a written recommendation with the numbers, the parameter set, the failure modes, and the draft SCR-058 methodology text handed to E24-D03 and E24-S07.

## Out of scope
Production implementation (E24-S07); the exact-cluster grouping of `cluster_window_ms` on `/market/liquidations`, which is not an estimate and is implemented in E24-T03; any rule-engine consumption of zones (excluded by NFR).

## Acceptance criteria
```gherkin
Scenario: Methods measured
  Given at least three recorded symbol-days including one cascade
  When each candidate method is evaluated
  Then a hit-rate and a false-positive rate is recorded per method with its parameters

Scenario: A recommendation with a default
  Then the spike recommends one method, or recommends shipping only the realised-liquidation histogram
  And states the default parameter values and confirms the feature is off by default

Scenario: Claims are bounded
  Then the spike produces the exact sentences SCR-058 may use, including the statement that Bybit publishes no per-account leverage or liquidation-price data

Scenario: No method is defensible
  Given every candidate performs no better than chance on the fixtures
  Then the recommendation is to ship only the exact realised-liquidation histogram, US-DERIV-007's estimated overlay is descoped with a recorded disposition, and E24-S07 is re-scoped rather than built on a method we cannot defend

Scenario: Cost is known
  Then the per-update compute cost of the chosen method is recorded in milliseconds against the bar-grid update rate
```

## Technical notes / design
Analysis runs offline in DuckDB over the Parquet cold tier plus the QuestDB `open_interest`, `liquidations` and `tickers` tables - no production code path. Where a risk-limit tier is unavailable the method must degrade explicitly rather than assume a value. The report must state, for each input, whether it is exchange-published or assumed. Time-box: 3 days.

## Test plan
Reproducible notebook/script committed under `research/` with the fixture ids; another engineer must be able to re-run it and obtain the same numbers.

## Security notes
This spike is the epic's principal integrity control: it decides whether we publish an inference at all. Findings feed E24-X02's abuse cases ("can a user be led to trade on a number we invented?"). No credentials or account data are touched - public market data only.

## Accessibility notes
N/A - no UI. The wording it produces is, however, the source of the accessible description for CMP-227 on the zones overlay.

## Performance notes
Records the compute cost per update so E24-S07 can be budgeted against the SCR-054 2 ms/frame scripting limit.

## Observability
Recommends the metric names the eventual implementation should emit (zone recompute duration, zone count) so observability is designed in.

## Definition of Done
- [ ] All candidate methods evaluated on >=3 symbol-days.
- [ ] Written recommendation with numbers, parameters and failure modes.
- [ ] Draft SCR-058 text delivered to E24-D03.
- [ ] Compute budget recorded and handed to E24-S07.
- [ ] Architect review comment recorded; time-box respected.

## Dependencies

title: Open-interest ingest, REST backfill and /market/open-interest endpoint
body:
## Context
The OI pane (US-DERIV-001, Must) needs two things the platform does not yet have: a continuously extended high-resolution OI series derived from the recorded `tickers` stream, and a REST backfill of the exchange's own 5min..1d OI history. Both land in the QuestDB `open_interest` table (`docs/plan/21-database-schema.md` §4.7) whose dedup key is `(ts, symbol, interval, source)` precisely so the two cadences can coexist without one overwriting the other. This task is backend only; the pane is E24-S01.

## Scope / Deliverables
- **Ingest path (M4):** extract `open_interest` / `open_interest_value` from the merged ticker snapshot produced by E08 and write `interval='1s'`, `source='ws_ticker'` rows to `open_interest`, downsampled to at most 1 row/second/symbol.
- **Backfill job (M4):** page Bybit `GET /v5/market/open-interest` (limit <=200/page, cursor paging) for the intervals `5min|15min|30min|1h|4h|1d`, writing `source='rest'` rows. Idempotent: re-running over a covered range produces no duplicates thanks to the dedup key.
- Backfill is triggered on first subscription to a symbol's OI and on demand for a requested range; concurrency limited per symbol; retries with exponential backoff and jitter; honours the shared Bybit rate-limit budget and error code 10018.
- **Endpoint:** implement `GET /api/v1/market/open-interest` exactly per `docs/plan/22-api-openapi.yaml` (`symbol`, `interval` default `5min`, `from`, `to`, `cursor`, `limit`; `x-rbac` `marketdata:read`), returning `{t, open_interest, open_interest_value}` items plus the standard `Page` meta with `next_cursor`, `has_more`, `count`.
- The response must disclose which source each point came from and the coverage window, so the client can render the "native granularity 5 min" note and never silently mix cadences.
- Range and limit caps per the E24-X01 model, rejecting oversized requests with 422.

## Out of scope
The pane and its rendering (E24-S01); OI delta and quadrant computation (E24-T04/E24-S02); funding (E24-T02); liquidations (E24-T03).

## Acceptance criteria
```gherkin
Scenario: Live extension
  Given a subscribed symbol whose ticker stream is flowing
  Then open_interest rows with interval='1s' and source='ws_ticker' are written at no more than one row per second per symbol

Scenario: Backfill paging
  Given a requested range covering more than 200 points at 5min granularity
  When the backfill runs
  Then it pages with the cursor until complete, writes source='rest' rows, and a second run over the same range writes no duplicate rows

Scenario: Backfill failure does not stop live data
  Given the Bybit REST call returns 5xx or rate-limit code 10018
  Then the job retries with backoff, the failure is logged with symbol, interval, attempt and http_status, live ws_ticker rows keep being written, and the endpoint reports the gap in its coverage meta rather than fabricating points

Scenario: Endpoint contract
  When GET /api/v1/market/open-interest?symbol=BTCUSDT&interval=5min&from=..&to=.. is called with a marketdata:read token
  Then the response validates against the OpenAPI schema, points are ascending by t, and the meta reports next_cursor, has_more and count

Scenario: Oversized request
  When a range or limit beyond the documented cap is requested
  Then the endpoint returns 422 with the standard error envelope and issues no query against QuestDB

Scenario: Unauthorised
  When the endpoint is called without a token or without marketdata:read
  Then it returns 401 or 403 respectively
```

## Technical notes / design
Backfill is a supervised asyncio task per (symbol, interval) with a bounded work queue, reusing the exchange-adapter's `fetch_open_interest(symbol, interval, ...)` method declared in `docs/plan/24-internal-schemas.md`. Writes go through the existing QuestDB ILP writer used by the recorder; the dedup key makes at-least-once delivery safe. Query side uses a parameterised SQL selection on `(symbol, interval, source)` with `ts` bounds - never string interpolation. Coverage meta is computed from `min(ts)`/`max(ts)` for the requested `(symbol, interval)` so the client can distinguish 'no data recorded' from 'zero OI'.

## Test plan
Unit: downsampler (1 Hz cap, monotonic ts), cursor paging loop, backoff schedule, idempotent re-run, coverage-meta computation. Contract: schema test for the endpoint against `22-api-openapi.yaml` incl. the 401/403/422 responses. Integration: recorded Bybit fixtures for a normal session, a paged backfill >200 rows, a 5xx sequence and a 10018 rate-limit sequence. Coverage >=85% on the new modules.

## Security notes
Threats from E24-X01: (D) unbounded range/limit - mitigated by the caps tested above; (T) source confusion - mitigated by persisting and returning `source` per point; (I) endpoint must keep `marketdata:read`. Public market data only; no secrets. Upstream frames are schema-validated before write so a malformed push cannot poison the table.

## Accessibility notes
N/A - backend only.

## Performance notes
Endpoint p95 <150 ms backend-internal (budget #13) for a 1 000-point page; ingest adds <1 ms per ticker frame; backfill runs off the hot path and must not delay live writes. Record both numbers in the ticket.

## Observability
Metrics `deriv_oi_backfill_pages_total{symbol,interval,result}`, `deriv_oi_backfill_latency_seconds`, `deriv_oi_rows_written_total{source}`. Structured warning log on backfill failure with `symbol`, `interval`, `attempt`, `http_status`. One trace span per backfill job.

- [ ] Unit tests added; coverage >=85% backend/engine, >=80% frontend on touched files.

title: Funding-rate service, interval resolution and /market/funding endpoint
body:
## Context
US-DERIV-003 (Must) and US-DERIV-004 (Should) hinge on one rule stated verbatim in `docs/plan/22-api-openapi.yaml`: "The funding interval is instrument-specific (`funding_interval_minutes`; 8 h common, some 1/2/4 h) - never assume 8 h." The interval drives the countdown, the annualisation factor and the `funding_8h` session anchor. This task makes the interval a resolved input everywhere and ships the settled-history plus predicted-rate service.

## Scope / Deliverables
- **Interval resolution:** read `funding_interval_minutes` from the instruments-info cache (`GET /api/v1/instruments/{symbol}`, Postgres `instruments.funding_interval_min`, column default 480) and expose a single accessor used by every consumer. A static analysis / grep check in CI asserts no other hard-coded 480 or 8-hour constant exists in the derivatives code.
- **Settled history:** backfill Bybit `GET /v5/market/funding/history` (limit <=200, cursor paging) into QuestDB `funding_rates` (`ts`, `symbol`, `funding_rate`, `annualised_pct`, `interval_min`, `source`), computing `annualised_pct = funding_rate * (525600 / interval_min) * 100` at write time.
- **Predicted rate:** the current unsettled rate is available only from the ticker `funding_rate` field; expose it flagged `predicted: true, estimated: true` and never persist it as a settled row. When absent, the API returns no predicted item at all so the client can show `n/a` rather than a stale value (US-DERIV-004 scenario 3).
- **Next settlement:** `next_funding_time_ms` from the ticker, served alongside so the client countdown needs no local schedule arithmetic beyond the clock offset.
- **Endpoint:** `GET /api/v1/market/funding` per the OpenAPI contract, returning `funding_interval_minutes` at the top level and items `{t, funding_rate, predicted, estimated}` with `Page` meta; `x-rbac` `marketdata:read`; range/limit caps.

## Out of scope
The funding UI, the countdown widget and the annualisation toggle (E24-S03/E24-S04); metric-descriptor registration (E24-T04); funding cost against real positions (E41).

## Acceptance criteria
```gherkin
Scenario: Interval comes from instrument data
  Given a symbol whose instruments-info funding_interval_minutes is 240
  When the funding history and the predicted rate are served
  Then funding_interval_minutes is 240 in the response and annualised_pct uses 525600/240, not 525600/480

Scenario: No hard-coded interval
  When the CI guard scans the derivatives backend modules
  Then no literal 480 or 8-hour funding constant exists outside the instruments table column default, and a violation fails the build

Scenario: Predicted is distinct and never persisted
  Then the current unsettled rate is returned with predicted=true and estimated=true
  And no row with predicted=true is written to funding_rates

Scenario: Predicted unavailable
  Given the ticker publishes no funding rate for the symbol
  Then the response contains no predicted item and the client can render n/a rather than a stale value

Scenario: History paging
  Given a range spanning more than 200 settlements
  Then the service pages with the cursor to completion and a re-run writes no duplicates

Scenario: Contract and authorisation
  Then the response validates against 22-api-openapi.yaml, and a caller without marketdata:read receives 403
```

## Technical notes / design
`annualised_pct` is precomputed at write time so queries stay cheap and so there is exactly one implementation of the formula. Settlement timestamps are stored as the exchange's settlement time; the dedup key `(ts, symbol)` makes the backfill idempotent. The interval accessor returns the instrument value or raises if the instrument is unknown - it must not silently fall back to a default at runtime, because a wrong interval produces a wrong countdown and a wrong annualisation simultaneously.

## Test plan
Unit: annualisation across 1 h/2 h/4 h/8 h intervals; the interval accessor's raise-on-unknown behaviour; predicted-rate flagging; paging and idempotence. Contract: OpenAPI schema test incl. `funding_interval_minutes` presence and the 403 case. Integration: recorded fixtures for an 8 h symbol and a 4 h symbol, plus a settlement boundary crossing. CI guard test for the constant scan. Coverage >=85%.

## Security notes
(T) presenting a predicted rate as settled is the epic's top misrepresentation threat; mitigated at the schema level (`predicted`/`estimated` are required in the response shape, not optional decoration) and asserted in E24-X02's flag-stripping abuse case. (D) range/limit caps as per E24-X01. Public data only.

## Accessibility notes
N/A - backend only.

## Performance notes
Endpoint p95 <150 ms backend-internal (budget #13). Funding data is low-cardinality; the whole visible history of a symbol fits comfortably in one page at most chart ranges.

## Observability
Metrics `deriv_funding_refresh_total{symbol,result}`, `deriv_funding_backfill_pages_total`, `deriv_funding_interval_minutes{symbol}` (gauge, so a wrong interval is visible in Grafana). Warning log when a symbol's interval is missing from the instruments cache.

title: Liquidation socket, persistence and /market/liquidations endpoint
body:
## Context
US-DERIV-005 (Must) needs forced-flow prints in real time, and US-DERIV-006 (Must) needs them bucketed per bar. Bybit's `allLiquidation.{symbol}` topic is the only source (the legacy `liquidation` topic is retired) and **there is no REST history endpoint at all** - `docs/plan/21-database-schema.md` §4.6 states depth is strictly bounded by recorder uptime and the UI must say so. This task owns the socket, the persistence, the WS republication and the local-history endpoint, including the coverage metadata that makes the partial-history state possible.

## Scope / Deliverables
- **Socket (M4):** subscribe `allLiquidation.{symbol}` through the public-stream connection manager from E08 for every recorded or auto-recorded symbol; normalise to the domain event and write to QuestDB `liquidations` (`ts`, `recv_ts`, `symbol`, `side`, `price`, `size`, `notional`, `stream='all'`) with dedup key `(ts, symbol, side, price, size)`.
- **WS republication:** publish `liquidations.{symbol}` and the multi-symbol `liquidations` topic per `docs/plan/23-ws-protocol.md` §14.9 `LiquidationBatch`, honouring the 500 ms throttle, the **append-never-merge** delivery rule for this topic, and the options `min_notional_usd` and `cluster_window_ms`. The `note` field stating that Bybit batches at most one push per symbol per 500 ms (so counts are lower bounds) is always populated.
- **Exact clustering:** `cluster_window_ms` groups prints within a time window into one item with `cluster_size` - this is exact grouping, not an estimate, and must never carry an `estimated` flag.
- **Endpoint:** `GET /api/v1/market/liquidations` per the OpenAPI contract (`symbol`, `from`, `to`, `cursor`, `limit`, `side`, `min_notional_usd`, `cluster_window_ms` 0..60000), reading only the local table.
- **Coverage metadata:** every response reports the recorder's first available timestamp for the symbol so the client can render the partial-history chip and the boundary marker (US-DERIV-006 scenario 3), and a query for a window entirely before that timestamp reports the coverage window rather than returning an innocent empty list.
- Recorder policy: `stream_kind` value `liquidations` registered so retention and the recorded-symbol list cover it (E16).

## Out of scope
The feed and bars UI (E24-S05/E24-S06); the estimated zone overlay (E24-K01/E24-S07); alerts on liquidations (E40).

## Acceptance criteria
```gherkin
Scenario: Prints persist and republish
  Given the allLiquidation topic is flowing for BTCUSDT
  Then each print is written to the liquidations table and republished on liquidations.BTCUSDT within the 500 ms throttle
  And the payload validates against the LiquidationBatch schema with the lower-bound note populated

Scenario: Append never merge
  Given three prints arrive inside one throttle window
  Then all three are delivered in the batch array and none is coalesced away

Scenario: Exact clustering
  Given cluster_window_ms=1000 and five prints inside one second
  Then they are returned as one item with cluster_size=5 and no estimated flag anywhere in the payload

Scenario: Coverage is stated
  Given the recorder for BTCUSDT started 2 hours ago
  When a 24-hour range is requested
  Then the response returns only the recorded window and reports the first available timestamp in its meta

Scenario: Query entirely outside coverage
  Given a range that ends before the recorder's first record
  Then the response reports the coverage window and an explicit no-coverage indication, not a bare empty success that would read as zero liquidations

Scenario: Cascade burst
  Given 500 prints per second for 10 seconds
  Then no print is lost between socket and table, the WS fan-out stays inside the throttle, and ingest lag stays under 1 second

Scenario: Reconnect
  Given the public socket drops mid-cascade
  Then it resubscribes automatically, the gap is logged, and duplicate prints replayed by the exchange are absorbed by the dedup key
```

## Technical notes / design
Normalisation maps the Bybit payload to the domain event defined in `docs/plan/24-internal-schemas.md`; `notional` is computed at ingest (price*size) so both the endpoint and the engine read one number. `side` is the side of the liquidated position's closing order, documented in the endpoint description - keep the field comment in code to stop it being re-interpreted. Writes use the recorder's ILP path with backpressure; a bounded queue drops nothing but applies backpressure to the socket reader rather than growing without limit. Multi-symbol `liquidations` subscriptions are capped at the protocol's symbol limit.

## Test plan
Unit: normaliser, notional computation, clustering by window, coverage-meta computation, dedup behaviour on replayed prints. Contract: `LiquidationBatch` JSON-schema validation and the REST schema test incl. 422 for `cluster_window_ms` > 60000. Integration: recorded fixtures - normal session, a cascade burst, a socket drop with replay, a symbol with no coverage. Perf: the 500 prints/s for 10 s ingest soak (also exercised end-to-end in E24-Q03). Coverage >=85%.

## Security notes
(D) cascade-driven fan-out amplification - mitigated by the 500 ms throttle, the batch shape and the subscription symbol cap; (D) unbounded history queries - range/limit caps; (T) an empty result being read as 'no liquidations happened' - mitigated by the explicit coverage metadata, which E24-X02 tests as an abuse case; (S) malformed upstream frames rejected by schema validation before write. Public market data only.

## Accessibility notes
N/A - backend only, but the coverage metadata is what makes the accessible partial-history disclosure possible downstream.

## Performance notes
Ingest lag <1 s under 500 prints/s; WS tick->screen p95 <100 ms with this topic in the heaviest set (budget #3, hard R2 gate); endpoint p95 <150 ms per page (budget #13).

## Observability
Metrics `deriv_liquidation_prints_total{symbol,side}`, `deriv_liquidation_notional_total{symbol,side}`, `deriv_liquidation_burst_rate{symbol}`, `deriv_liquidation_ingest_lag_seconds`, `deriv_liquidation_socket_reconnects_total`. Warning log on socket drop with the gap duration.

title: DerivativesEngine and metric-descriptor registration in the MetricRegistry
body:
## Context
The single-source invariant of R2 is that a pane, a `/market/metrics` query and a rule condition read the same number. `docs/plan/24-internal-schemas.md` §7 already fixes the derivatives descriptors: `open_interest`, `open_interest_value`, `open_interest_delta` (`OI(close) - OI(open)` per bar), `oi_price_quadrant` (`long_buildup|short_covering|short_buildup|long_unwind`), `funding_rate`, `funding_annualized`, `time_to_funding_ms`, `basis`, `premium_pct` (params `source=last|mark`), `liquidation_notional` (params `side=long|short|both`). This task implements the one engine in M9 that produces them and registers them so every consumer is a renderer, not a calculator.

## Scope / Deliverables
- `server/orderflow/derivatives.py`: a pure `DerivativesEngine` taking `(ticker snapshots, OI rows, funding rows, liquidation prints, bar grid, instrument metadata)` and returning metric series. No HTTP, no socket, no QuestDB code inside it.
- Implement each descriptor above with its documented formula: `open_interest_delta` per bar from the OI series resampled onto the bar grid; the quadrant truth table; `funding_annualized = funding_rate * (525600 / funding_interval_minutes)`; `basis = last - index` (or `mark - index` when `source=mark`), `premium_pct = basis / index * 100`; `time_to_funding_ms` from `next_funding_time_ms` and the synced clock offset; `liquidation_notional` bucketed per bar and split by side, aligned to the bar grid and the UTC day boundary.
- **The None case is first-class:** a bar with no OI sample yields `open_interest_delta = None` and `oi_price_quadrant = None`; it is never defaulted to zero or to a quadrant (US-DERIV-002 scenario 3).
- Register every descriptor in the `MetricRegistry` with unit, params, bar-scoping and the `estimated` flag (all of these are `estimated: false`; only the E24-S07 zone overlay is estimated), and wire them into `GET /api/v1/market/metrics` alongside the already-declared codes `open_interest_delta`, `funding_basis` and `liquidation_intensity`.
- Expose the derivatives fields on the `ticker.{symbol}` WS payload per `23-ws-protocol.md` §14.8 (`open_interest`, `open_interest_value`, `funding_rate`, `next_funding_time_ms`, `mark_price`, `index_price`, `stale`).
- Incremental update path: on a new ticker snapshot or liquidation print, only the current bar's metrics are recomputed, not the whole window.

## Out of scope
Rendering (E24-S01..S08); the estimated liquidation-zone computation (E24-S07, which uses the E24-K01 method and is flagged estimated); alert/rule consumption (E40/E35, which only require the descriptors to exist).

## Acceptance criteria
```gherkin
Scenario: One number everywhere
  Given the engine has computed open_interest_delta and basis for BTCUSDT bar 10:35
  When the SCR-054 pane, a GET /api/v1/market/metrics query and a rule condition each read those metrics
  Then all three return identical values for the same bar and params

Scenario: Quadrant truth table
  Given price up and OI up, price up and OI down, price down and OI up, price down and OI down
  Then the classification is long_buildup, short_covering, short_buildup and long_unwind respectively

Scenario: Missing OI is not a quadrant
  Given a bar for which no OI sample exists
  Then open_interest_delta and oi_price_quadrant are both None, and the bar is excluded from classification rather than defaulted

Scenario: Annualisation follows the instrument
  Given funding_interval_minutes is 240
  Then funding_annualized equals funding_rate multiplied by 525600/240

Scenario: Liquidation bucketing
  Given prints spanning a UTC day boundary on a 1h bar grid
  Then liquidation_notional buckets align to the bar grid and the day boundary, split by side, with no print counted twice or dropped

Scenario: Registry completeness
  When the MetricRegistry is enumerated
  Then all ten derivatives descriptors from 24-internal-schemas.md section 7 are present with unit, params and estimated flag, and a registry test fails if one is missing

Scenario: Incremental update
  Given a new ticker snapshot for the current bar
  Then only the current bar's metrics are recomputed and the result is identical to a full recompute over the window
```

## Technical notes / design
Decimal handling follows the platform convention (string-decimals on the wire, exact types internally) so a basis of 0.1 does not become 0.09999999. The bar grid is supplied by the bar builders (E12) - the engine never builds bars. Resampling OI onto a coarser bar grid uses last-value-at-or-before semantics with an explicit staleness bound; beyond the bound the sample is absent, which routes into the None case rather than carrying an old value forward indefinitely. The engine is deterministic given its inputs - a property E24-T06 exploits for the golden-fixture parity harness.

## Test plan
Unit: quadrant truth table incl. None; annualisation at 1 h/2 h/4 h/8 h; basis and premium for both sources; per-bar liquidation bucketing incl. the day boundary and the side split; countdown arithmetic against a skewed clock offset; resampling staleness bound; incremental-vs-full-recompute equivalence as a property test. Contract: `/market/metrics` schema test for each derivatives code; `TickerUpdate` schema validation. Integration: recorded symbol-day producing a full metric set. Coverage >=85% on `server/orderflow/derivatives*`.

## Security notes
(T) the `estimated` flag must be a property of the descriptor, not of the caller - the registry test asserts it; (R) each OI point retains its `source` so a displayed value is attributable. No secrets, no PII. Inputs come from already-validated internal stores, so the engine may assume schema validity but must still reject NaN/infinite inputs rather than propagating them into a rendered number.

## Accessibility notes
N/A - backend/engine. The descriptors' `unit` field is what the UI's table alternatives and accessible names are built from, so units must be correct and human-meaningful.

## Performance notes
`deriv_engine_compute_seconds{metric}` p95 <5 ms per incremental update for a visible window of 1 500 bars; a full recompute of that window <50 ms. Both recorded in the ticket. The engine is on the path to budget #3 (WS tick -> screen p95 <100 ms).

title: Golden-fixture parity harness for derivatives metrics vs offline DuckDB
body:
## Context
R2's exit criteria require order-flow values to be provably correct, not merely plausible: a recorded symbol-day recomputed offline must match what the live engine produced. This epic's numbers (OI delta, quadrant, annualised funding, basis, per-bar liquidation notional) are exactly the kind that look right while being subtly wrong - an off-by-one bar boundary or a carried-forward stale OI sample is invisible on a chart. The harness makes that class of bug a failing test.

## Scope / Deliverables
- An independent reference implementation of each derivatives metric as SQL over the Parquet cold tier in DuckDB, written from `docs/plan/24-internal-schemas.md` §7 rather than from the engine's code, so it is a genuine second opinion.
- A harness that replays a recorded symbol-day through the `DerivativesEngine` and diffs every metric series against the reference within a declared float tolerance, reporting the first divergent bar with both values.
- Coverage of the awkward cases in the fixture set: a bar with no OI sample; a funding settlement inside the window; a symbol with a non-8 h funding interval; a liquidation cascade; a UTC day boundary; a recorder gap.
- Determinism check: replaying the same fixture twice produces identical output, and an incremental replay matches a full recompute.
- Wired into CI as a scheduled (not per-PR) job because it is minutes-long, with a per-PR fast subset over a short fixture.

## Out of scope
Black-box functional testing (E24-Q01/Q02); load and cascade performance (E24-Q03); the estimated zone overlay, which has no ground truth to compare against and is validated by E24-K01's backtest instead.

## Acceptance criteria
```gherkin
Scenario: Parity on a recorded symbol-day
  Given a recorded BTCUSDT symbol-day replayed through the engine
  When every derivatives metric series is diffed against the DuckDB reference
  Then all series match within the declared tolerance and the job passes

Scenario: A divergence is actionable
  Given an injected off-by-one in the bar bucketing
  Then the harness fails and names the metric, the first divergent bar timestamp and both values

Scenario: Awkward cases included
  Then the fixture set contains a no-OI bar, a funding settlement, a 4-hour-interval symbol, a cascade, a UTC day boundary and a recorder gap, each asserted explicitly

Scenario: Determinism
  When the same fixture is replayed twice
  Then the outputs are byte-identical, and an incremental replay matches a full recompute

Scenario: CI wiring
  Then the full harness runs on a schedule and a fast subset runs per PR, and a failure of either blocks the release train
```

## Technical notes / design
Reference SQL lives under `tests/golden/e24/` next to the fixture manifest. Tolerance is declared per metric (exact for counts and classifications such as `oi_price_quadrant`; a small relative epsilon for floating-point ratios such as `premium_pct`) - a classification metric must match exactly, since 'nearly the right quadrant' is meaningless. Fixtures are referenced by id from the shared recorded-fixture store established in E16, not copied into the repo.

## Test plan
The harness is itself the test; it is validated by mutation - deliberately perturbing the engine (shifted bar boundary, carried-forward OI, 8 h interval assumption) must make it fail. Those mutation cases are committed as expected-fail tests.

## Security notes
Detects silent data-integrity regressions, which is the epic's primary risk; a persistent unexplained divergence is treated as a security-relevant integrity finding and escalated to E24-X02 rather than quietly re-baselined.

## Accessibility notes
N/A

## Performance notes
The scheduled job must complete within the CI budget for long jobs; the per-PR subset must add <2 minutes to the pipeline. Record both.

## Observability
Publishes a per-metric divergence count as a CI artefact so slow drift is visible across runs rather than only on a hard failure.

title: Render the open-interest sub-pane on SCR-054 with backfill and gap states
body:
## Context
Implements **US-DERIV-001 - Open interest pane (Must)**: "OI renders in a linked sub-pane, backfilled from REST and updated from the tickers stream". This is the first surface of SCR-054 and establishes the pane scaffolding (CMP-186 OiFundingLiqPane) the funding and liquidation sub-panes then slot into. All numbers come from the `DerivativesEngine` via `/market/metrics` and `ticker.{symbol}`; the client computes nothing.

## Scope / Deliverables
- The OI sub-pane inside CMP-186 on SCR-054, hosted as a linked chart-engine sub-pane sharing the price pane's time axis (CMP-188 PriceAxis) and crosshair sync (US-DERIV-008 NFR).
- Backfill on mount via `GET /api/v1/market/open-interest?symbol&interval&from&to`, then live extension from `ticker.{symbol}` (`open_interest`, `open_interest_value`).
- Interval alignment: points align to bar boundaries; when the chart interval is finer than the REST native granularity, render the "Native granularity 5 min" note from the E24-D05 copy deck (US-DERIV-001 scenario 2).
- Gap and failure states: a backfill failure renders the missing history as an explicit gap with a retry action carrying `last_success_at`, while live OI keeps streaming (US-DERIV-001 scenario 3); never a blank pane.
- Header readout via CMP-036 KeyValueRow (current OI with unit and the 1 h change), pane legend via CMP-199 ChartLegend, collapse/expand persistence.
- Stale shading after 2 s without an expected update (global convention #4) with the last-good timestamp visible.
- Table alternative: an accessible table of the visible OI points with timestamp, value and unit.
- Analytics: `oi_panel.metric_toggled`, `oi_panel.interval_changed`.

## Out of scope
OI delta and quadrant colouring (E24-S02); funding (E24-S03/S04); liquidations (E24-S05..S07); basis (E24-S08); the endpoint and engine (E24-T01/T04).

## Acceptance criteria
```gherkin
Scenario: Backfill then live
  Given I open SCR-054 for BTCUSDT on a 5m chart
  Then historical OI is fetched and drawn, and subsequent ticker updates extend the series live without a refetch

Scenario: Interval alignment and the granularity note
  Given the chart is on 1m and the REST native granularity is 5 min
  Then points align to bar boundaries and the pane shows the native-granularity note

Scenario: Backfill failure
  Given the backfill request fails
  Then live OI still streams, the missing history renders as an explicit gap rather than a straight line, a retry action is offered, and the last successful timestamp is shown

Scenario: Stale data
  Given no ticker update arrives for more than 2 seconds
  Then the pane is shaded stale and the last-good timestamp is displayed, and the shading clears on the next update

Scenario: No history recorded
  Given the symbol has never been recorded and the exchange returns no history
  Then the pane shows the designed empty state naming the recording start, not a blank canvas

Scenario: Table alternative
  When I open the pane's table alternative with the keyboard
  Then the visible OI points are listed with timestamps, values and units, and it is reachable without a pointer

Scenario: No client-side computation
  When the pane renders any derived value
  Then it originates from the engine response, and the client performs no arithmetic beyond formatting
```

## Technical notes / design
The sub-pane is created through the chart engine's pane API (`docs/plan/26-chart-engine-design.md`), sharing the time scale so pan/zoom and crosshair are automatic rather than re-implemented. title: OI delta mode and OI/price quadrant classification on the OI sub-pane
body:
## Context
Implements **US-DERIV-002 - OI delta and price quadrant colouring (Should)**: per-bar OI change classified by price direction so build-ups and squeezes are legible at a glance. The classification itself is `oi_price_quadrant` from the engine (E24-T04); this story is the control surface and the rendering, including the case that most often gets faked - a bar with no OI sample.

## Scope / Deliverables
- Absolute/delta toggle for the OI sub-pane, persisted per user in Postgres `settings` (scope `user`, key `deriv.oi.mode`, values `absolute|delta`).
- Delta mode renders per-bar `open_interest_delta` as a histogram aligned to the bar grid.
- Quadrant colouring toggle (`deriv.oi.quadrant_colouring`) applying the four styles from E24-D03: `long_buildup`, `short_covering`, `short_buildup`, `long_unwind` - each with a distinct **pattern** as well as colour, plus a text legend in CMP-199 ChartLegend naming all four in words.
- A bar with no OI sample renders neutral-hatched and is excluded from classification; the legend states how many bars in view are unclassified.
- Crosshair readout showing the bar's delta and its quadrant name in text.
- Table alternative gains delta and quadrant columns.
- Analytics: `oi_panel.metric_toggled` with the new mode.

## Out of scope
Computing the delta or the quadrant (E24-T04); alerts on quadrant transitions (E40); funding and liquidation panes.

## Acceptance criteria
```gherkin
Scenario: Quadrant classification renders
  Given price and OI both rose on a bar
  Then the bar is drawn in the long_buildup style with its distinct pattern, and the legend names long_buildup in words

Scenario: All four quadrants
  Given bars covering price-up/OI-up, price-up/OI-down, price-down/OI-up and price-down/OI-down
  Then they render as long_buildup, short_covering, short_buildup and long_unwind, each visually distinct in greyscale

Scenario: Absolute versus delta
  When I switch to delta-per-bar
  Then the pane shows the change rather than the level, and the preference survives a reload and a new session

Scenario: Missing OI for a bar
  Given no OI sample exists for a bar
  Then it is drawn neutral-hatched, is excluded from classification, and the legend reports the count of unclassified bars in view

Scenario: Colour is never the only encoding
  When the pane is viewed in greyscale or with a colour-vision-deficiency simulation
  Then every quadrant remains distinguishable by pattern and the legend text

Scenario: Crosshair readout
  When I place the crosshair on a classified bar
  Then the readout shows the delta with its unit and the quadrant name as text
```

## Technical notes / design
The component receives `open_interest_delta` and `oi_price_quadrant` series and maps quadrant enum values to style tokens through a single lookup table taken from the E24-D03 spec - no conditional colour logic scattered through the renderer. `None` is a first-class value in that lookup, mapping to the neutral hatch. Setting writes go through the existing settings API and emit the standard `settings.change` audit entry.

## Test plan
Unit: enum-to-style mapping incl. None; unclassified-bar counting; settings persistence and restore. Component/Storybook: all four quadrants, mixed window, all-unclassified window, delta vs absolute. Visual regression on the four styles in greyscale. E2E in E24-Q02. Coverage >=80%.

## Security notes
No new surface. The integrity rule is that the client must not infer a quadrant when the engine returned None - E24-Q01 includes a negative test for exactly that.

## Accessibility notes
Quadrants are conveyed by pattern + text legend, never colour alone (WCAG 1.4.1); the toggle is a labelled control with a visible focus ring; the table alternative gains quadrant names as text; the unclassified count is announced politely when it changes materially, not on every frame.

## Performance notes
Delta mode adds no per-frame computation - the series is precomputed server-side. Pattern fills must use the engine's existing instanced-geometry path so 1 500 bars do not cost 1 500 draw calls; measure and record the frame time against budget #1.

## Observability
Analytics `oi_panel.metric_toggled` with `{mode, quadrant_colouring}`; a counter of unclassified bars rendered, so a systematic OI gap shows up in telemetry as well as on screen.

title: Funding rate, stepped history and second-accurate settlement countdown
body:
## Context
Implements **US-DERIV-003 - Funding rate, history and countdown (Must)**. Its NFR is exacting: "countdown accurate to the second using the synced clock offset", and scenario 3 demands the funding interval be read from instrument metadata and used everywhere, including session anchors. The countdown appears twice - in the symbol header and in the SCR-054 funding sub-pane - and both must be the same component instance's output, not two timers.

## Scope / Deliverables
- Funding sub-pane in CMP-186: settled funding history over the chart's time range, rendered as a stepped line or bars (`deriv.funding.style`, persisted per user), on the shared time axis.
- CMP-126 FundingCountdown in the symbol header and in the sub-pane, driven by `time_to_funding_ms` from the engine plus the synced clock offset (E17's clock sync), ticking to the second.
- Imminent-settlement warning at <5 min using the E24-D05 copy, including the estimated charge line where a position exists ("Funding settles in 04:12 - position will be charged ~12.40 USDT"); with no position the charge line is omitted rather than showing zero.
- Interval correctness: the symbol's `funding_interval_minutes` is displayed and used for the history step width and the countdown target; a 4 h symbol renders six settlements a day.
- States: history loading, no settled history yet, source failure with retry and `last_success_at`, stale shading.
- Table alternative for the funding history with settlement timestamps, rates and units.
- Analytics: `funding.countdown_alert_set`.

## Out of scope
Predicted and annualised display (E24-S04); the funding service and interval resolution (E24-T02); funding cost accounting against realised positions (E41 Journal); alerts on funding thresholds (E40).

## Acceptance criteria
```gherkin
Scenario: Current rate and countdown
  Given BTCUSDT is subscribed
  Then the current funding rate and the time to next settlement render in the symbol header and in the funding sub-pane, both showing the same value

Scenario: Second accuracy under clock skew
  Given the local clock is 3 seconds ahead of the exchange
  Then the countdown uses the synced clock offset and reaches zero within one second of the true settlement time

Scenario: History uses the instrument's interval
  Given a symbol whose funding interval is 4 hours
  Then the stepped history shows six settlements per day and the interval is stated in the pane, with no 8-hour assumption anywhere

Scenario: Imminent settlement
  Given less than 5 minutes remain
  Then the warning state renders with the copy from the handoff pack, and the estimated charge line appears only when a position exists

Scenario: Source failure
  Given the funding history request fails
  Then the pane shows a retry state with the last successful timestamp rather than a blank chart, and the countdown keeps running from the last known next-settlement time

Scenario: Settlement rollover
  When the countdown reaches zero
  Then the pane requests the newly settled rate, appends it to the history, and restarts the countdown for the next interval without a manual refresh

Scenario: Announcement policy
  When a screen reader is active
  Then the countdown is announced at 5 minutes and at 1 minute remaining only, never every second
```

## Technical notes / design
One countdown source of truth: a single store entry derived from `time_to_funding_ms` and the clock offset; the header and the pane both subscribe to it, so they cannot drift. The tick is driven by a single interval timer shared across all countdowns, not one timer per instance. Step width for the history comes from `funding_interval_minutes` in the `/market/funding` response - never from the spacing between observed points, which would silently break on a missing settlement.

## Test plan
Unit: countdown arithmetic against a skewed offset; rollover at zero; step-width derivation; imminent-threshold transitions; retry-state rendering. Component/Storybook: CMP-126 Positive, Negative, UnderOneMinute; CMP-186 FundingOnly with 8 h and 4 h symbols. Integration: a fixture crossing a settlement boundary. E2E in E24-Q02. Coverage >=80%.

## Security notes
A wrong countdown or a wrong interval misleads a user about a real cost, so this is an integrity-relevant surface even though it holds no secrets. The interval must come from instrument metadata; the CI guard from E24-T02 prevents a re-introduced constant.

## Accessibility notes
Countdown announced at 5 min and 1 min only (SCR-054 catalogue entry); the countdown's accessible name states what it counts down to; rate sign is conveyed by text and the CMP-020 NumericText contract, not by colour alone; table alternative for the history; visible focus on the style toggle.

## Performance notes
The countdown re-renders only its own text node once per second; the funding series redraws on change only (<=1 Hz data). Shared timer keeps per-frame cost near zero. Measure against the SCR-054 2 ms/frame budget.

## Observability
Analytics `funding.countdown_alert_set`; a client error event on funding fetch failure; a warning when the clock offset exceeds a threshold, since that directly degrades countdown accuracy.

title: Predicted and annualised funding with explicit non-settled styling
body:
## Context
Implements **US-DERIV-004 - Predicted and annualised funding (Should)** whose NFR is a hard rule: "never present predicted values styled as settled". The annualised figure is what traders actually compare across symbols, and it is only meaningful when computed with the symbol's own interval - which is why the tooltip must show the formula with the actual factor in it.

## Scope / Deliverables
- Annualisation toggle (`deriv.funding.annualised`, persisted per user) switching the displayed rate and the history series between the per-interval rate and `funding_annualized` from the engine.
- Tooltip showing the formula with the symbol's real numbers: `rate x (525600 / {funding_interval_minutes}) = {annualised}`.
- Predicted (unsettled) rate rendered in the distinct style specified by E24-D03 - distinguishable in greyscale - with a text label "predicted" and a CMP-227 EstimatedBadge linking SCR-058.
- When no predicted rate is published, the field shows "n/a" (never a stale or carried-forward value), and the history shows no phantom point.
- Table alternative gains an annualised column and a settled/predicted column as text.

## Out of scope
The funding service and the predicted flag itself (E24-T02); the countdown (E24-S03); cross-symbol funding comparison screens.

## Acceptance criteria
```gherkin
Scenario: Annualised toggle
  When I enable annualisation
  Then rates display annualised using the symbol's own funding interval, and the tooltip shows the formula with that interval substituted

Scenario: Annualisation is interval-correct
  Given a symbol funding every 4 hours with a rate of 0.0001
  Then the annualised value uses the factor 525600/240 and not 525600/480

Scenario: Predicted is visually and textually distinct
  Then the predicted next rate is rendered in a style distinguishable in greyscale, carries the word predicted in text, and shows an (estimated) badge linking the methodology drawer

Scenario: Predicted unavailable
  Given no predicted rate is published for the symbol
  Then the field shows n/a, no point is added to the history, and no previously seen predicted value is reused

Scenario: Toggle persistence
  When I reload the app
  Then the annualisation preference is restored, and the tooltip still shows the correct formula for the current symbol

Scenario: Screen reader
  When the predicted value is read out
  Then its accessible name contains both predicted and estimated as words
```

## Technical notes / design
Both the rate and the annualised value come from the engine's descriptors (`funding_rate`, `funding_annualized`); the client never multiplies.
