title: Liquidation feed with burst coalescing and recorder-bounded history disclosure
body:
## Context
Implements **US-DERIV-005 - Liquidation feed (Must)**: each event shows side, size, price and time, the pane states that no historical liquidation endpoint exists, and a cascade of hundreds of events per second coalesces per frame with a burst rate shown. The honesty requirement here is structural: an empty feed must never be readable as "no liquidations happened" when it actually means "we were not recording".

## Scope / Deliverables
- Liquidation feed surface on SCR-054: a virtualised list of prints with side (as text, not only colour), size, price, notional and time, fed by `liquidations.{symbol}` (`LiquidationBatch`) with `min_notional_usd` as a subscription option.
- Backfill of the visible window from `GET /api/v1/market/liquidations`, reading local recorder data only.
- Burst handling: prints are coalesced into 250 ms buckets with a visible burst-rate counter ("1 240 prints/s"), never one DOM node per print; the pane states that Bybit batches at most one push per symbol per 500 ms so counts are lower bounds.
- Partial-history state: an explicit chip naming the first available timestamp and stating that no exchange history endpoint exists for liquidations, from the E24-D05 copy deck; shown whenever the requested window starts before the recorder's coverage.
- CMP-127 LiquidationMarker on the chart for prints above the threshold, with the DOM-mirror pattern for accessibility.
- Click-through: `liquidation.print_clicked` analytics and crosshair sync to the print's timestamp.
- Table alternative: the feed itself is a table with headers and units, so the accessible alternative is the primary structure rather than a bolt-on.

## Out of scope
Per-bar bucketing into bars (E24-S06); estimated zones (E24-S07); the socket, persistence and endpoint (E24-T03); liquidation alerts (E40); the user's own position liquidation line (E31/E32).

## Acceptance criteria
```gherkin
Scenario: Feed renders prints
  Given the liquidations topic is subscribed for BTCUSDT
  Then each event shows side, size, price, notional and time, with side stated in text

Scenario: No REST history is disclosed
  Then the pane states that no historical liquidation endpoint exists and that history is limited to the recorder's runtime

Scenario: Partial history chip
  Given the recorder for BTCUSDT started 2 hours ago and I request a 24-hour window
  Then a chip names the first available timestamp and the feed shows only the recorded window

Scenario: Empty is never mistaken for zero
  Given the requested window is entirely outside the recorder's coverage
  Then the pane shows the no-coverage state explaining why it is empty, and does not display an empty list that would read as no liquidations

Scenario: Cascade
  Given hundreds of events per second during a cascade
  Then prints are coalesced into 250 ms buckets, a burst-rate counter is displayed, no frames are dropped, and the DOM node count stays bounded

Scenario: Threshold filter
  Given min_notional_usd is set
  Then smaller prints are excluded server-side via the subscription option and the active filter is stated in the pane

Scenario: Announcements under load
  When a screen reader is active during a cascade
  Then at most one summary announcement every 5 seconds naming the burst rate is made, not one per print
```

## Technical notes / design
The list is virtualised with a fixed-size ring buffer of recent prints; the coalescing buffer flushes on the animation frame following the 250 ms window, so render work is decoupled from arrival rate. `min_notional_usd` is applied as a subscription option so filtering happens server-side and the wire is not saturated during a cascade. The partial-history condition compares the requested window against the coverage metadata returned by E24-T03 - it is never inferred from 'the oldest row we happened to receive'.

## Test plan
Unit: coalescing buffer (bucket boundaries, burst-rate computation), ring-buffer eviction, partial-history condition, filter-state rendering. Component/Storybook: CMP-186 LiquidationBars/feed states - populated, cascade, partial, no-coverage, filtered. Perf: 500 prints/s for 10 s with scripting <2 ms/frame (full script in E24-Q03). E2E in E24-Q02. Coverage >=80%.

## Security notes
(D) client-side cascade amplification - mitigated by coalescing and the bounded buffer; (T) an empty feed misread as zero liquidations - mitigated by the no-coverage state, tested as an abuse case in E24-X02.

## Accessibility notes
Feed is a real table with headers and units; side is text; burst announcements are throttled to one per 5 s per E24-D04's policy; CMP-127 markers use the DOM-mirror pattern so sparse events are reachable by keyboard; visible focus on rows; contrast >=4.5:1.

## Performance notes
SCR-054 budget: <=2 ms scripting per frame during a cascade of 500 prints/s sustained for 10 s with no dropped frames; DOM nodes bounded regardless of print rate; WS tick -> screen p95 <100 ms (budget #3, hard R2 gate).

## Observability
Analytics `liquidation.print_clicked`; client metrics for coalesced-bucket count and observed burst rate; an error event when the backfill request fails.

title: Per-bar liquidation bars split long/short with threshold and history boundary
body:
## Context
Implements **US-DERIV-006 - Liquidation bars (Must)**: per-bar long and short liquidation notional as a split histogram, with a minimum-notional filter stated in the legend and an explicit boundary marker where the recorder's history begins. The NFR - "bucketing aligns to the chart interval and the day boundary" - is satisfied by the engine's `liquidation_notional` descriptor (E24-T04); this story renders it honestly.

## Scope / Deliverables
- Split histogram in the liquidation sub-pane: long and short notional per bar, drawn from `liquidation_notional` with `side=long|short`, aligned to the chart's bar grid and the shared time axis.
- Side labelling in text on the axis/legend, so long versus short is never colour-only.
- Minimum-notional filter (`deriv.liq.min_notional_usd`, persisted per user) applied server-side; the active threshold is stated in CMP-199 ChartLegend (US-DERIV-006 scenario 2).
- Bars/heatmap mode selector (`deriv.liq.mode`) with bars as the default; the heatmap variant is the realised-liquidation density from recorded prints (exact), not the estimated zone overlay of E24-S07.
- History boundary marker: a vertical boundary at the recorder's first available timestamp with a label, so the absence of bars before it is explained on the chart itself (US-DERIV-006 scenario 3).
- Crosshair readout of a bar's long and short notional with units.
- Table alternative gains per-bar long/short columns.

## Out of scope
The estimated liquidation-zone overlay (E24-S07); the print feed (E24-S05); bucketing computation (E24-T04); alerts.

## Acceptance criteria
```gherkin
Scenario: Split histogram
  Then per-bar long and short liquidation notional render as a split histogram with both sides labelled in text

Scenario: Bucketing alignment
  Given a 1h chart spanning a UTC day boundary
  Then buckets align to the bar grid and to the day boundary, with no print counted twice or dropped

Scenario: Threshold filter
  When I set a minimum notional
  Then smaller events are excluded and the active filter is stated in the legend

Scenario: Empty history boundary
  Given the recorder started 2 hours ago
  Then bars exist only for that window and an explicit boundary marker labels the first available timestamp

Scenario: Zero versus unknown
  Given a bar inside the recorded window with no liquidations
  Then it renders as a genuine zero, visually distinct from bars before the recording boundary which render as unknown

Scenario: Mode switch
  When I switch between bars and the realised-density heatmap
  Then the same underlying recorded data is shown, the mode persists, and neither mode is labelled estimated
```

## Technical notes / design
Series come from `/market/metrics` with `metric=liquidation_notional` and `params={"side":"long"}` / `"short"`, on the chart's bar type and parameter, so the bar grid is guaranteed identical to price. The boundary marker position comes from the coverage metadata (E24-T03), not from the first non-empty bucket. Zero and unknown are separate states in the data model and must remain separate in the renderer - this is the story's main correctness trap.

## Test plan
Unit: zero-versus-unknown rendering decision; legend threshold text; boundary-marker placement from coverage metadata; mode persistence. Component/Storybook: populated, filtered, boundary-in-view, all-unknown, cascade bar. Integration: fixture spanning a day boundary. E2E in E24-Q02. Coverage >=80%.

## Security notes
(T) presenting 'no recorded data' as 'no liquidations' - mitigated by the zero/unknown distinction and the boundary marker, both tested by E24-X02 and E24-Q01.

## Accessibility notes
Sides labelled in text; the boundary marker has a text label readable by a screen reader; the table alternative distinguishes zero from unknown with words, not blanks; contrast >=3:1 for the bar fills against the pane background.

## Performance notes
Bars are a static series per view; redraws only on new bars or a threshold change. Frame time p95 <=16.6 ms with the full scene (budget #1); the histogram must use the engine's instanced path.

## Observability
Analytics on threshold and mode changes; a counter of renders showing the boundary marker, which indicates how often users look past their recording depth.

title: Estimated liquidation zones: off by default, acknowledged, badged and disclosed
body:
## Context
Implements **US-DERIV-007 - Liquidation heat / cluster estimate (Should)**, the epic's most dangerous feature. Its NFR is absolute: "never presented as exchange-provided data; excluded from any automated rule action by default". The screens catalogue makes a missing `(estimated)` badge a P1 bug, not a cosmetic one. E24-K01 decides the method and may recommend descoping the overlay entirely - this story implements whatever K01 concluded, including the descope path.

## Scope / Deliverables
- Zone overlay on the price pane rendering the bands produced by the method chosen in E24-K01, from a descriptor registered as `estimated: true`.
- **Off by default** (`deriv.liq.zones_enabled` default `false`). Enabling requires an acknowledgement dialog stating the value is an estimate derived from aggregate OI and assumed leverage tiers, not exchange data; the acknowledgement is recorded as an audit event.
- CMP-227 EstimatedBadge on every zone and in the pane legend, focusable, opening SCR-058's liquidation-cluster section by Enter or click.
- SCR-058 content wired: the method, its inputs (and which are assumed rather than published), the thresholds in force, the known failure modes, and the sentence "this is an estimate, not exchange-provided fact".
- Explicit exclusion from automated actions: the descriptor is flagged so the rule engine will not accept it as a condition input by default, and the UI states this where zones are configured.
- Descope path: if E24-K01 concluded no method is defensible, this story ships the realised-liquidation density only (already exact, from E24-S06), records the descoping on the epic, and removes the toggle rather than shipping a disabled stub.

## Out of scope
The estimation method itself (E24-K01 decides it; E24-T04 hosts the computation); the exact `cluster_window_ms` grouping, which is not an estimate (E24-T03); rule-engine integration (E35).

## Acceptance criteria
```gherkin
Scenario: Disabled by default
  Given a fresh installation
  Then liquidation zones are off, and no zone geometry is requested or rendered

Scenario: Enabling requires acknowledgement
  When I enable zones
  Then a dialog states that the values are estimated and not exchange-provided, enabling only proceeds after explicit acknowledgement, and the acknowledgement is written to the audit log

Scenario: Badge on every zone
  Given zones are enabled
  Then every zone and the pane legend carry an (estimated) badge whose accessible name contains the word estimated, and each badge opens the methodology drawer

Scenario: Methodology disclosure
  When I open the methodology drawer from a zone badge
  Then it describes the method, its inputs, which inputs are assumed rather than exchange-published, the thresholds in force and the known failure modes

Scenario: Missing badge is a P1
  Given a build in which a zone renders without its badge
  Then the automated catalogue-level badge test fails and the build is rejected

Scenario: Not available to automated actions
  When a rule condition attempts to use the zone metric
  Then it is rejected by default with an explanation, and no rule can act on an estimated zone without an explicit override

Scenario: Method descoped
  Given E24-K01 concluded no method is defensible
  Then the overlay is not shipped, the toggle is absent rather than disabled, the realised-liquidation density remains available, and the descoping is recorded on the epic
```

## Technical notes / design
The overlay reads a single `estimated: true` descriptor; the badge is rendered from that flag, not from a hard-coded prop, so a future non-estimated series would not silently inherit the badge and an estimated one cannot lose it. The acknowledgement is persisted per user in `settings` and emits a `settings.change` audit entry with the acknowledged text version, so we can prove what the user agreed to if the copy later changes. Zone geometry is recomputed only on the cadence E24-K01 measured, never per frame.

Unit: default-off behaviour; acknowledgement gate; badge presence bound to the descriptor flag; rule-engine rejection path. Catalogue-level test (CMP-227's own contract): every surface rendering an estimated series renders the badge. Component/Storybook: zones off, acknowledgement dialog, zones on with badges, descoped build. Negative: flag stripped from the payload must not yield an unbadged zone (shared with E24-X02). E2E in E24-Q02. Coverage >=80%.

## Security notes
This is the epic's principal misrepresentation control (E24-X01 threat (T)). Controls: default-off, an acknowledgement with an audit trail, a schema-level estimated flag driving the badge, mandatory methodology disclosure, and exclusion from automated actions. Reviewed and abuse-tested in E24-X02; a missing badge is treated as a security finding, not a UI defect.

## Accessibility notes
CMP-227 is focusable, its accessible name contains the literal word "estimated", and it opens SCR-058 by Enter; zones are distinguishable without colour (pattern + labelled legend); the acknowledgement dialog is a focus-trapped, keyboard-operable dialog; the overlay never obscures price data below the contrast floor.

## Performance notes
Zone geometry is recomputed at the cadence measured in E24-K01 and drawn as a small number of instanced bands; the overlay must add <1 ms per frame and must not increase the SCR-054 total beyond its 2 ms/frame budget. Record the measured cost.

## Context
Implements **US-DERIV-008 - Basis, mark/index and long/short ratio (Should)**. Its NFR governs the whole epic: "all derivative series respect the same time axis and crosshair sync as price", and scenario 3 fixes the failure behaviour: a failed source shows a retry state with the last successful timestamp, never a blank chart.

## Scope / Deliverables
- Basis readout and series: mark, index and their spread from the engine's `basis` and `premium_pct` descriptors, with the `source=last|mark` selector (`deriv.basis.source`) and an annualised-basis toggle (`deriv.basis.annualised`), all persisted per user.
- Rendering on the shared time axis with crosshair sync, as a peer sub-pane or a header readout per the E24-D05 decision; values via CMP-036 KeyValueRow with units.
- Global long/short account ratio rendered at its native period with the period stated in words (e.g. "5 min, exchange-published"); if the platform's adapter cannot supply it for USDT perps, the surface states the source is unavailable rather than showing a fabricated series, and the limitation is recorded in E24-T05.
- Retry state: when a source fails, show the last successful timestamp and a retry action; never a blank chart (US-DERIV-008 scenario 3).
- Table alternative covering mark, index, basis, premium and the ratio with units and periods.
- Crosshair readout of basis and premium at the hovered bar.

## Out of scope
Computing basis/premium (E24-T04); OI, funding and liquidation panes; options/GEX (out of scope for the product); funding-cost accounting (E41).

## Acceptance criteria
```gherkin
Scenario: Basis pane
  Then mark, index and their spread render together, with an annualised basis toggle and units on every figure

Scenario: Source selector
  When I switch the basis source from last to mark
  Then the series and the readout recompute server-side, the selection persists, and the active source is stated in the pane

Scenario: Long/short ratio
  Then the global account ratio renders at its native period with the period stated in words

Scenario: Source unavailable
  Given the ratio source fails
  Then the pane shows a retry state with the last successful timestamp, not a blank chart

Scenario: Ratio not published
  Given the exchange publishes no long/short ratio for this instrument
  Then the surface states that the source is unavailable rather than rendering an empty or fabricated series

Scenario: Axis and crosshair sync
  When I pan, zoom or move the crosshair on the price pane
  Then the basis series follows the same time axis and the crosshair readout updates in lockstep with price

Scenario: No client-side computation
  Then basis, premium and the annualised basis all originate from the engine, and the client performs no arithmetic beyond formatting
```

## Technical notes / design
Basis and premium are read from `/market/metrics` with the `source` param, and live values from the `ticker.{symbol}` `mark_price`/`index_price` fields; the two paths must agree, which the golden-fixture harness (E24-T06) checks. The pane registers with the chart engine's shared time scale so sync is structural rather than event-forwarded. The retry state stores `last_success_at` in the view model so it survives re-renders.

## Test plan
Unit: source-selector state and persistence; retry-state rendering and last-success tracking; unavailable-source path; formatting with units. Component/Storybook: populated, source=mark, annualised, retry, unavailable. Integration: fixture where the ratio source 5xxs. E2E in E24-Q02, including a pan/zoom sync assertion. Coverage >=80%.

## Security notes
(T) an unavailable source must not be rendered as zero or as a flat line - both would be fabricated data; the unavailable and retry states are the mitigation and are covered by E24-X02's abuse cases.

## Accessibility notes
Every figure carries its unit in the accessible name; the period of the ratio is stated in words; the retry action is a labelled button with visible focus; the table alternative includes all five values; sign of basis is conveyed by text as well as colour.

## Performance notes
Low-frequency data (<=1 Hz); render on change only. The pane must not add a second time-scale computation - it reuses the shared scale, keeping frame time inside budget #1.

## Observability
Analytics on source and annualisation toggles; a client error event with the status on source failure; a counter of retry-state renders.

title: Estimated liquidation zones (K01 method a): acknowledged, badged and disclosed
body:
## Context
The (a) half of **US-DERIV-007 - Liquidation heat / cluster estimate (Should)**, split out of E24-S07 (#782). E24-S07 as written implemented the estimated-zones overlay, the epic's most dangerous feature (NFR: "never presented as exchange-provided data; excluded from any automated rule action by default"; a missing `(estimated)` badge is a P1 bug, not a cosmetic one). The E24-K01 finding (`docs/plan/spikes/E24-K01.md` section 1) scoped S07 to method **(b)**, the recorded-liquidation histogram, and held method **(a)**, the OI-weighted leverage-bucket projection, back: its leverage-tier mix is assumed rather than published (section 4), and the synthetic runs disagree with each other, so they cannot show that (a) beats chance.

Orchestrator ruling 6624627875 on #782 (BQ 1, NG-7) accepted that: **E24-S07 ships (b) only** (as drawn by D02 `zones-b-alone` and D03 S54-56 / S54-57: no acknowledgement, no CMP-227, no SCR-058 link), and builds none of (a), not even a dormant stub. The (a) scope, which is today's E24-S07 acceptance criteria 2-6, moves here. This story is **gated on the K01 real-data re-run** (the #1778 item A exception on E24-K01 #664 accepted the synthetic corpus for the agent-delivery phase; the re-run on at least 3 recorded symbol-days including a liquidation cascade is owed when the recorder has captures). K01 section 1 item 2 states the rule: reopen (a) as an opt-in overlay only if the re-run shows a hit rate of at least chance + 0.05 and at least 0.8x of (b); otherwise (a) stays descoped and this story is retired, not built.

`24` section 6.4 still says predicted/estimated liquidation levels are "not in v1"; this story is the later phase it names, and its contract slice amends that paragraph first.

## Scope / Deliverables
Exactly the (a) items, none of them started before the gate in Dependencies is met:
- **Estimated bands on the price pane**, from a descriptor registered as `estimated: true`: hatched bands (`pattern.hatch.estimated`, a dashed outline, never a solid fill and never a buy/sell hue), each labelled like `82,400-82,520 (estimated)`. The bands are computed server-side (E24-T04 hosts the computation) from aggregate open interest, the instruments-info risk-limit / MMR tiers and the assumed leverage-tier mix (K01 section 4); with the tiers absent the layer degrades explicitly (no band), and the geometry is recomputed only at the cadence the K01 re-run measures, never per frame.
- **Off by default** (`deriv.zones_enabled`, client default `false`: the leaf #5699 declares and ruling 6624627875 BQ 3 reserves for (a), with the `24` section 19 note S07's contract slice adds). The settings row reads "Estimated zones (assumed leverage)" with "Off by default. An estimate, not exchange data. Not available to rules." (D02 `zones-off`, D03 S54-52).
- **The enable dialog and the acknowledgement leaf**: turning the row on opens CMP-044 (standard) titled "Show estimated zones?" with the (a) copy of D02 section 7 / D03 S54-53 verbatim, `Cancel` as initial focus; the acknowledged text version is stored per user in `settings` (a new leaf, `deriv.zones_ack_version` PROPOSED, contract-first in `22` / `24` / `21`) and written as a `settings.change` audit event; an acknowledgement of an older text version is not carried over, the dialog re-opens before zones next show.
- **CMP-227 EstimatedBadge** on every band (`marker`) and in the pane legend (`inline`), focusable, detector `liquidation_cluster` (adding that member to `22` `DetectorMethodology.detector` is this story's contract slice, D03-G5), opening SCR-058's "Liquidation cluster (estimated)" section by Enter or click. The badge renders from the descriptor's `estimated` flag, never from a hard-coded prop.
- **The SCR-058 link and the (a) copy**: the section's content is E25-T07's (#798) and its drawer E25-S04's (#794) (hand-off HO-7); this story wires the badge to it, emits `methodology.opened` with `{detector: "liquidation_cluster"}`, and uses the (a) strings of D02 section 7 / D03 sections 7 and 14 verbatim, passing K01 section 6a's forbidden-phrase check (no "estimated liquidation levels", no "liquidation zones" without "recorded").
- **Exclusion from automated actions**: the descriptor is flagged so the rule engine refuses it as a condition input by default (the producer register entry of E35-T15, #5745: marked `estimated` or unavailable), and the UI states "Estimated zones are not available to rules." where zones are configured.
- **Viewer and view-as on the switch**: T2 "disabled with a visible reason" for a Viewer (the acknowledgement is audited, so no session-only mode) and, under view-as, T2 `rbac.view_as` pointing at the popover's one notice (D02 `zones-viewer`, D03 S54-54 and T2-1, `.claude/rules/32-design-specs.md` G-T2).
- **The table alternative** `table-zones` (D03 S54-69): From (USDT), To (USDT), Label `(estimated)`, with "Not available to rules." above it.

## Out of scope
- **Method (b), "Recorded liquidations by price"**: E24-S07 (#782) ships it (ruling 6624627875): the `deriv.liq_by_price` leaf, the by-price read, the toggle and legend row, the K01 section 6a copy. CMP-227 is never shown on that exact data.
- **The rule engine's use of estimated metrics**: the explicit override, the vocabulary registry's handling of `estimated` confidence, and the `liquidation_cluster_distance` mismatch (registered `exact` in `services/api/candleviewer/rules/vocabulary/metrics.py`, estimated in `24`) belong to E35 and the E24-X02 (#785) G-row. This story only makes the zone descriptor refusable and tests that the refusal holds once E35's register carries it.
- **The K01 real-data re-run itself**: an E24-K01 follow-up on the recorder's captures, run through `docs/plan/spikes/E24-K01-harness/`; this story starts after it, not as part of it.
- The SCR-058 drawer and its content (E25-S04, E25-T07); the engine's hatched-band encoder where the engine epic has not landed it (an engine G-row, no engine code here); the exact `cluster_window_ms` grouping, which is not an estimate (E24-T03); any order placing, sizing or timing derived from a band.

## Acceptance criteria
Scenarios 2-6 are E24-S07's former acceptance criteria 2-6, re-keyed to the (a) layer; scenario 1 replaces S07's former "Disabled by default" for the layer that is labelled estimated; scenario 7 is the gate.
```gherkin
Scenario: Off by default and labelled estimated
  Given a fresh installation
  Then estimated liquidation zones are off, no band geometry is requested or rendered, and the settings row reads "Estimated zones (assumed leverage)" with "Off by default. An estimate, not exchange data. Not available to rules."
  And once enabled, the layer's legend row carries the same words and an (estimated) badge

Scenario: Enabling requires acknowledgement
  When I enable zones
  Then a dialog states that the bands are an estimate from aggregate open interest and assumed leverage tiers, not exchange data, enabling only proceeds after explicit acknowledgement, and the acknowledged text version is written to the audit log as a settings.change event
  And an acknowledgement of an older text version is not carried over: the dialog re-opens before zones next show

Scenario: Badge on every band
  Given zones are enabled
  Then every band and the pane legend carry an (estimated) badge whose accessible name contains the word estimated, rendered from the descriptor's estimated flag, and each badge opens SCR-058's Liquidation cluster (estimated) section by Enter or click

Scenario: Methodology disclosure
  When I open the section from a band badge
  Then it describes the method, its inputs, which inputs are assumed rather than exchange-published, the thresholds in force and the known failure modes

Scenario: Missing badge is a P1
  Given a build in which a band renders without its badge, or a payload with the estimated flag stripped
  Then the automated catalogue-level badge test fails and the build is rejected, and a stripped payload is refused and draws nothing

Scenario: Not available to automated actions
  When a rule condition attempts to use the zone metric
  Then it is rejected by default with an explanation, and no rule can act on an estimated zone without an explicit override

Scenario: Gate on the K01 real-data re-run
  Given the K01 re-run on at least 3 recorded symbol-days including a cascade has not shown a hit rate of at least chance + 0.05 and at least 0.8x of the recorded histogram
  Then no (a) code ships, the toggle is absent rather than disabled, no dormant stub exists, and the descoping is recorded on the epic
```

## Design-ahead waiver (Architect/CDO) — explicit record
No waiver is taken. The (a) frames are drawn, behind the stamp "Method (a) held back by E24-K01 section 1 item 2 · off by default · not built until the real-data re-run":
- **E24-D02** (`docs/design/E24/E24-D02.md` section 7, boards 15 and 16): `SCR-054/zones-off`, `zones-acknowledgement`, `zones-viewer`, `zones-enabled` (and `zones-k01-recorded` for (b), which is S07's).
- **E24-D03** (`docs/design/E24/E24-D03.md`): section 7 rows S54-52 `zones-off`, S54-53 `zones-acknowledgement`, S54-54 `zones-viewer`, S54-55 `zones-enabled`; S54-69 `table-zones`; T2-1 (the switch); section 14 (the SCR-058 section "Liquidation cluster (estimated)", stamped not built until the re-run); section 15.4 (the CMP-227 `liquidation_cluster` bindings).
- **Still PROPOSED / open at filing**, to be listed in the PR description: the `liquidation_cluster` member of `22` `DetectorMethodology.detector` (D03-G5); the `deriv.zones_ack_version` leaf name and the acknowledged text-version scheme; the metric names under Observability; the D03 boards (issue #661, boards PENDING) and the E24-D05 hand-off (#663), which were still open when the E24-S07 BQ list was read on 2026-11-04.
- At pickup the implementer re-reads both specs and the design tickets' status. If a design ticket is not Done, the Definition of Ready (C-11.1) fails and the story is blocked, not waived. The planned sprint (Sprint 21) is 11 sprints after D02 (Sprint 10) and 10 after D03 (Sprint 11), which satisfies the design-ahead lead time of `docs/plan/02-definition-of-ready-done.md` section 3.1.

## Technical notes / design
- **Slices (proposed)**, each at most about 1,500 counted lines (C-4.8), `Refs` plus `Partial:` until the last: (0) contract first (C-6.1): `22` (the estimated-zones read or descriptor with a required `estimated` field, the acknowledgement leaf, `DetectorMethodology.detector` + `liquidation_cluster`), `24` section 6.4 (replace the "not in v1" sentence) and section 19, regenerated protocol types; (1) the server computation behind E24-T04's descriptor; (2) web data, model, dialog, badges, legend, table alternative, T2; (3) engine attach and close.
- **The flag drives the badge.** The layer model reads the required `estimated` field and renders CMP-227 iff `true`; S07's (b) layer ships `false` through the same model, so this story reuses it. A payload with the field stripped is refused by the decoder and draws nothing (the shared negative with E24-X02).
- **The acknowledgement** is persisted per user in `settings` and emits a `settings.change` audit entry carrying the acknowledged text version, so we can prove what the user agreed to if the copy later changes. `PATCH /settings` needs `settings:write`; RBAC is enforced server-side, the T2 state is only its rendering.
- **Recompute cadence** is the one the K01 real-data re-run measures (its pure-Python timings are not a budget, K01 section 6); never per frame.
- **No client estimation**: the client renders server bands only (C-2.12); no client-side re-bucketing or leverage arithmetic.

## Test plan
Unit: default-off behaviour; the acknowledgement gate including the older-text-version re-prompt; badge presence bound to the descriptor flag; the decoder refusing a stripped flag; the zone metric refused by the rule vocabulary register (E35-T15's entry); the T2 reasons for a Viewer and under view-as. Catalogue-level test (CMP-227's own contract): every surface rendering an estimated series renders the badge. ## Context
`docs/plan/03-testing-strategy.md` requires a black-box plan per feature group alongside the white-box review. This epic's defects are mostly *semantic* - a number that is plausible but wrong, or an absence that reads as a zero - so the plan is written from the eight DERIV stories' acceptance criteria and from the E24-X01 abuse cases rather than from the implementation.

## Scope / Deliverables
- A test plan covering all eight US-DERIV stories: per story, the happy path, the documented edge cases, and the failure cases, each with the fixture needed and the expected observable result.
- The semantic checks that automation alone will miss: zero versus unknown in liquidation bars; predicted versus settled funding; `ws_ticker` versus `rest` OI provenance; a quadrant never invented for a bar without an OI sample; a countdown that stays correct across a settlement rollover and a clock-offset change; an interval of 4 h honoured everywhere including the session anchor.
- Negative tests derived from E24-X01: oversized ranges, missing permissions, flag-stripped payloads, coverage-less liquidation queries.
- An exploratory charter (session-based, 2 x 90 min) with a stated mission: "find a place where the panel implies data we do not have", plus a second charter for the cascade behaviour.
- Defect taxonomy and severity rules for this epic: a missing `(estimated)` badge or a fabricated value is P1; a wrong unit is P1; a spacing deviation is P3.
- Test data plan: which recorded fixtures are needed (normal session, cascade, funding settlement, 4 h-interval symbol, recorder gap, backfill failure) and how each is produced.

Automation (E24-Q02 E2E, E24-Q03 perf); a11y audit (E24-Q04); the design sweep (E24-D06); unit tests, which live with their stories.

title: Cascade load script and perf benchmark for the derivatives surfaces
body:
## Context
The SCR-054 catalogue entry sets a specific, testable budget: liquidation prints coalesce into 250 ms buckets and the panel must not exceed **2 ms scripting per frame** during a cascade of **500 prints/s sustained for 10 s with no dropped frames**. Budget #3 (WS tick -> screen p95 <100 ms) is a hard R2 gate and must still hold with `ticker` and `liquidations` in the heaviest topic set. This ticket builds the scripts that prove both, and the chaos scenarios around them.

## Scope / Deliverables
- A load generator producing the cascade profile (500 prints/s for 10 s, with a ramp and a burst variant at 1 000 prints/s for 2 s) into the WS fan-out, reusing the k6/Locust harness from `docs/plan/06-performance-and-load-standard.md`.
- A browser-side benchmark capturing per-frame scripting time, dropped frames, DOM node count and memory during the cascade with SCR-054 open alongside the heaviest R2 scene.
- End-to-end WS tick -> screen latency measurement with the full topic set including `ticker` and `liquidations`, reporting p95 and p99.
- Backend measurements: liquidation ingest lag under cascade; `/market/open-interest`, `/market/funding` and `/market/liquidations` p95 at a full page; `deriv_engine_compute_seconds` p95 for incremental updates.
- Chaos scenarios: ticker socket drop and resubscribe mid-cascade; REST backfill failure during load; clock-offset jump during a running countdown; QuestDB write backpressure.
- Results recorded on this ticket and on the epic against the budget table; a regression threshold wired into the perf CI job.

## Out of scope
Functional E2E (E24-Q02); the golden-fixture correctness harness (E24-T06); optimisation work, which is raised as separate tickets if a budget is missed.

## Acceptance criteria
```gherkin
Scenario: Cascade budget
  Given 500 liquidation prints per second sustained for 10 seconds with SCR-054 open
  Then panel scripting stays under 2 ms per frame, no frames are dropped, and the DOM node count stays bounded

Scenario: Latency gate
  When WS tick to screen latency is measured with the heaviest topic set including ticker and liquidations
  Then p95 is under 100 ms and p99 under 250 ms

Scenario: Backend budgets
  Then each of the three history endpoints returns a full page with p95 under 150 ms backend-internal, and engine incremental compute p95 is under 5 ms

Scenario: Chaos - socket drop
  Given the ticker socket drops during a cascade
  Then the client shows stale shading within 2 seconds, resubscribes automatically, recovers without a reload, and no fabricated values appear during the gap

Scenario: Chaos - clock jump
  Given the clock offset jumps by 3 seconds while a countdown is running
  Then the countdown re-anchors to the synced offset within one tick rather than drifting or jumping backwards

Scenario: Budget missed
  Given any measured value exceeds its budget
  Then the run is recorded as a fail, a defect ticket is raised with the measurement, and the epic cannot reach Done on an unrecorded regression
```

## Technical notes / design
Load generation targets the WS fan-out directly so the exchange is never involved; the fixture is the recorded cascade day from E16. Browser measurements use the Performance API and the engine's existing FPS/scripting instrumentation from E11's benchmark harness, so numbers are comparable with other R2 epics. All runs are on the standard benchmark machine profile defined in `06-performance-and-load-standard.md`; ad-hoc laptops do not count.

## Test plan
The scripts are the deliverable; each is validated by an injected regression (an artificial 5 ms per-frame cost) which must make the run fail.

## Security notes
The cascade profile doubles as the DoS amplification test from E24-X01 threat (D); results are shared with E24-X02 rather than measured twice.

## Accessibility notes
Verifies that announcement throttling holds under load - a cascade must not produce a flood of live-region announcements, which is both an a11y and a performance failure.

## Performance notes
This ticket is the performance evidence for the epic DoD; budgets #1, #2, #3 and #13 plus the SCR-054-specific 2 ms/frame limit are all reported here.

## Observability
Runs export the `deriv_*` metrics to the benchmark dashboard so a later regression can be compared against this baseline.

title: Accessibility audit of SCR-054 and the derivatives table alternatives
body:
## Context
`docs/plan/05-accessibility-standard.md` requires WCAG 2.2 AA with axe-core in CI plus a manual screen-reader pass for every new screen. SCR-054 is unusually demanding: three canvas sub-panes each needing a table alternative, a countdown with a strict announcement policy, a burst surface needing announcement throttling, and honesty affordances whose entire point is that they must be perceivable non-visually.

## Scope / Deliverables
- axe-core automated audit wired into CI for SCR-054, the settings surface, the zone acknowledgement dialog and the SCR-058 drawer section.
- Manual screen-reader passes (NVDA on Windows and VoiceOver on macOS) against the checklist produced by E24-D04.
- Verify per sub-pane: a table alternative exists, is reachable by keyboard, and carries units and headers; the canvas is not the only disclosure of any value.
- Verify the countdown is announced at 5 min and 1 min only, never per second; verify cascade announcements are throttled to at most one summary per 5 s.
- Verify non-colour encoding: OI quadrants (pattern + text legend), liquidation side (text), basis sign (text), predicted versus settled funding.
- Verify CMP-227's accessible name contains the literal word "estimated" everywhere it appears, and that it is focusable and opens SCR-058 with Enter.
- Verify keyboard operation end to end with visible focus, including the acknowledgement dialog's focus trap and return-focus behaviour.
- Contrast measurement in both themes for text (>=4.5:1) and graphical boundaries (>=3:1).
- Findings logged with WCAG success-criterion references and severities; re-test after fixes.

## Out of scope
Design-time a11y review (E24-D04); functional E2E (E24-Q02); other screens.

## Acceptance criteria
```gherkin
Scenario: Automated audit clean
  When axe-core runs on SCR-054 and its dialogs in CI
  Then there are zero serious or critical violations

Scenario: Table alternatives complete
  Then each of the OI, funding and liquidation sub-panes and the basis readout has a keyboard-reachable table alternative with headers and units

Scenario: Announcement policy holds
  When the countdown runs and a cascade occurs
  Then the countdown is announced at 5 minutes and 1 minute only, and cascade announcements occur at most once every 5 seconds

Scenario: Nothing by colour alone
  When the panel is inspected in greyscale
  Then quadrant, liquidation side, basis sign and predicted-versus-settled remain distinguishable

Scenario: Estimated badge is perceivable non-visually
  When a screen reader encounters a zone or a predicted funding value
  Then the word estimated is spoken as part of the accessible name, and the badge can be activated by keyboard to open the methodology

Scenario: Contrast in both themes
  Then every text element measures at least 4.5:1 and every graphical boundary at least 3:1, in dark and light

Scenario: A violation is found
  Then it is logged with its WCAG success criterion and severity, fixed, and confirmed in a re-test before the epic can close
```

## Technical notes / design
Automated runs use the shared axe configuration; canvas surfaces are audited through their DOM mirrors, since axe cannot see pixels - the audit explicitly checks that the mirror exists and is complete rather than accepting a clean run over an empty DOM.

## Test plan
The audit is the test; evidence is the axe report, the screen-reader session recordings and the contrast measurements, all attached.

## Security notes
Overlaps E24-X02 on the badge assertion deliberately: provenance that is only visual is inaccessible, and inaccessible provenance is no provenance.

## Accessibility notes
This ticket is the a11y evidence for the epic DoD.

## Performance notes
Confirms the announcement throttling that protects both accessibility and the frame budget under cascade.

## Observability
N/A - findings are tracked as tickets.

- [ ] Manual NVDA and VoiceOver passes recorded.

- [ ] Contrast measured in both themes.

The epic DoD requires an epic-level regression and exploratory pass, not merely the sum of per-story QA. This ticket assembles the durable regression pack that later trains run, performs the final pass across all eight DERIV stories on a release-candidate build, and records the sign-off.
